SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t2.SUBJECT_CODE, t2.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(t2.SUBJECT_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t2.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t2 ON t1.TERM_CODE = t2.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE t2.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND t2.TOTAL_UNITS >= 6 AND t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), math_grad_students AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS total_graduate_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ), all_grad_students AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS total_graduate_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ), avg_grad_students AS ( SELECT AVG(total_graduate_students) AS avg_grad_students FROM all_grad_students ) SELECT icte.SUBJECT_CODE, icte.SUBJECT_NUMBER, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, icte.window_column, mgs.total_graduate_students, CASE WHEN mgs.total_graduate_students > ags.avg_grad_students THEN 'ABOVE_AVERAGE' WHEN mgs.total_graduate_students < ags.avg_grad_students THEN 'BELOW_AVERAGE' ELSE 'AVERAGE' END AS grad_student_status FROM inner_cte icte LEFT JOIN math_grad_students mgs ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = mgs.DEPARTMENT_NAME CROSS JOIN avg_grad_students ags ORDER BY icte.SUBJECT_CODE;

question: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year with a total of at least 6 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject code, subject number, department name, the running sum of subject codes within each department ordered by subject code, the total number of graduate students whose department is degree granting, whose student year is 'G', and who are in the Mathematics department, as well as the school name and department phone number for the Mathematics department. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT t2.SUBJECT_CODE, t2.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(t2.SUBJECT_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t2.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t2 ON t1.TERM_CODE = t2.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE t2.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND t2.TOTAL_UNITS >= 6 AND t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), math_grad_students AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, COUNT(msd.FULL_NAME) AS total_graduate_students FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN MIT_STUDENT_DIRECTORY msd ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = msd.DEPARTMENT WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND msd.STUDENT_YEAR = 'G' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT icte.SUBJECT_CODE, icte.SUBJECT_NUMBER, icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, icte.window_column, mgs.total_graduate_students, sd.SCHOOL_NAME AS school_name, ad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER AS department_phone FROM inner_cte icte LEFT JOIN math_grad_students mgs ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = mgs.DEPARTMENT_NAME LEFT JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT sd ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME LEFT JOIN SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT ad ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = ad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY icte.SUBJECT_CODE;

question: For each department (Chemistry or Biology) and academic year where the number of enrolled students in a subject is greater than 0, provide the count of subjects, the minimum start date of the term for that department and year, and the number of Mathematics subjects offered in the fall term for the same academic year (if it is among the top 10 years for Mathematics fall offerings). Additionally, show the average number of enrolled students per Chemistry/Biology subject for that department and year. Show the department, academic year, Chemistry/Biology subject count, minimum term start date, average enrolled students per subject, and Mathematics fall subject count, in that order. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME AS department, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS academic_year, COUNT(DISTINCT tso.SUBJECT_ID) AS subject_count, MIN(ata.TERM_START_DATE) AS min_term_start_date, AVG(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS avg_enrolled_students FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON tso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE WHERE tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 0 AND tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME IN ('Chemistry', 'Biology') GROUP BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR ), TopMathFallSubjects AS ( SELECT ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(so.SUBJECT_KEY) AS subject_count FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED so JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON so.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs ON at.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE WHERE ccs.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY subject_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT i.department, i.academic_year, i.subject_count AS chem_bio_subject_count, i.min_term_start_date, i.avg_enrolled_students, t.subject_count AS math_fall_subject_count FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN TopMathFallSubjects t ON i.academic_year = t.academic_year ORDER BY i.department, i.academic_year;

question: For each academic year, show the academic year, academic year description, and the highest total units for Mathematics subjects offered in regular terms that start after January 1, 2010, as well as the highest total units for Mathematics subjects offered in all regular terms, listing the columns in the following order: academic year, academic year description, highest total units (for terms after January 1, 2010), and highest total units (for all regular terms). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS highest_total_units_after_2010 FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND at.TERM_START_DATE > '2010-01-01' AND at.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) SELECT ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, ic.highest_total_units_after_2010, stats.highest_total_units_all_regular_terms FROM inner_cte ic JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR = at.ACADEMIC_YEAR JOIN ( SELECT at2.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(ccso2.TOTAL_UNITS) AS highest_total_units_all_regular_terms FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS at2 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso2 ON at2.TERM_CODE = ccso2.TERM_CODE WHERE at2.IS_REGULAR_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at2.ACADEMIC_YEAR ) stats ON ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR = stats.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY ic.ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For the Management department, list the department name, the title of the subject with the maximum number of students enrolled in any subject offered by that department in the 2022FA term (where the maximum enrollment is greater than 20), the maximum number of enrolled students, and for each subject offered in the academic year 2024 that is also present in the CIS course catalog, show the subject ID, subject code, subject number, department name, subject short title, subject title, lecture units, lab units, total units, grade type, grade rule, and the minimum total units value over each department code group, ordered by department code and subject ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, tso.SUBJECT_TITLE, tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS AS MAX_NUM_ENROLLED FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT sd JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE WHERE sd.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' AND tso.TERM_CODE = '2022FA' AND sd.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Management' AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = ( SELECT MAX(tso2.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) FROM TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tso2 WHERE tso2.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AND tso2.TERM_CODE = '2022FA' ) AND tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 20 ), MgmtSubjects2024 AS ( SELECT t0.SUBJECT_ID, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.LECTURE_UNITS, t0.LAB_UNITS, t0.TOTAL_UNITS, t0.GRADE_TYPE, t0.GRADE_RULE, min(t0.TOTAL_UNITS) OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS min_total_units_by_dept, t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG t1 ON t0.SUBJECT_ID = t1.SUBJECT_ID WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Management' ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ) SELECT icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME, icte.SUBJECT_TITLE AS MAX_ENROLL_SUBJECT_TITLE, icte.MAX_NUM_ENROLLED, ms.SUBJECT_ID, ms.SUBJECT_CODE, ms.SUBJECT_NUMBER, ms.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS MS_DEPARTMENT_NAME, ms.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, ms.SUBJECT_TITLE AS MS_SUBJECT_TITLE, ms.LECTURE_UNITS, ms.LAB_UNITS, ms.TOTAL_UNITS, ms.GRADE_TYPE, ms.GRADE_RULE, ms.min_total_units_by_dept FROM inner_cte icte JOIN MgmtSubjects2024 ms ON icte.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ms.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY ms.DEPARTMENT_CODE, ms.SUBJECT_ID;

question: For each department, provide the department name, the maximum, minimum, and average of the range of total units for subjects offered by that department in each term (considering only subjects with more than 0 total units and offered in the 'Engineering' school), and the highest maximum enrollment among IAP activities in 2021 that were not cancelled and were associated with subjects offered by that department. List the department name, max range across terms, min range across terms, avg range across terms, and highest max enrollment in that order. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte1 AS ( SELECT scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE, MAX(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) - MIN(sos.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_range FROM SIS_SUBJECT_CODE ssc JOIN SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION scd ON ssc.SUBJECT_CODE = scd.COURSE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY sos ON scd.COURSE = sos.COURSE_NUMBER WHERE sos.TOTAL_UNITS > 0 AND sos.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME = 'Engineering' GROUP BY scd.DEPARTMENT_NAME, sos.TERM_CODE ), DepartmentUnitsRange AS ( SELECT DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(total_units_range) AS max_range_across_terms, MIN(total_units_range) AS min_range_across_terms, AVG(total_units_range) AS avg_range_across_terms FROM inner_cte1 GROUP BY DEPARTMENT_NAME ), inner_cte2 AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS math_iap_activities_2021 FROM IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL isd JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON isd.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON ata.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2021 AND isd.IS_CANCELLED = 'N' AND isd.MAX_ENROLLMENT >= 20 AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ), DepartmentIAPMaxEnroll AS ( SELECT ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(isd.MAX_ENROLLMENT) AS highest_max_enrollment FROM IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL isd JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON isd.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON ata.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2021 AND isd.IS_CANCELLED = 'N' GROUP BY ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME ) SELECT dur.DEPARTMENT_NAME, dur.max_range_across_terms, dur.min_range_across_terms, dur.avg_range_across_terms, diae.highest_max_enrollment FROM DepartmentUnitsRange dur JOIN DepartmentIAPMaxEnroll diae ON dur.DEPARTMENT_NAME = diae.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY dur.max_range_across_terms DESC, diae.highest_max_enrollment DESC;

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with a total of 12 units in the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject number, subject title, department name, term description, and the rank of each subject within its department ordered by subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY t2 ON t1.TERM_CODE = t2.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: What is the minimum number of lecture units and the total sum of total units for subjects that are offered in the fall term, have a material status of 'U', and are in the Mathematics department? Please use data from the library reserve material details, academic terms, and course catalog subject offered tables. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT MIN(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) AS min_lecture_units, SUM(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units_sum FROM LIBRARY_RESERVE_MATRL_DETAIL lrm JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON lrm.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON ata.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE AND lrm.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID WHERE lrm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = 'U' AND ccso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics';

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2022 that are letter graded and are in the Mathematics department, show the subject title, department name, term description, and assign row numbers within a window of 2 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by subject title. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_TITLE ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND t0.GRADE_TYPE = 'L' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: What is the minimum number of lecture units and the sum of total units for all subjects that are offered in the fall term, where the subject has at least one associated textbook or material, the subject's department name is 'Mathematics', and the department code is '18'? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT MIN(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS min_lecture_units, SUM(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS sum_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN TIP_DETAIL t ON c.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID AND c.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE WHERE c.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = '18' AND t.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY IS NOT NULL AND t.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY <> '';

question: For subjects in the course catalog with a total of 12 units, offered in the fall term, and in the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject number, department name, subject title, total units, whether the subject is offered in the fall term, the offering department name, the subject enrollment number, and assign row numbers within each department ordered by subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.TOTAL_UNITS, t0.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM, t1.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, t2.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY t2 ON t1.TERM_CODE = t2.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t0.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 with a total of 12 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject code, subject title, department name, school name, and rank within each school name group ordered by subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t1.SUBJECT_CODE, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SCHOOL_NAME, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.SCHOOL_NAME ORDER BY t1.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM SIS_DEPARTMENT t0 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE = t1.DEPARTMENT_CODE WHERE t1.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t1.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2024 that are also present in the CIS course catalog and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject ID, subject code, subject number, department name, subject short title, subject title, lecture units, lab units, total units, grade type, grade rule, and the minimum total units value over each department code group, ordered by department code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_ID, t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME, t0.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t0.LECTURE_UNITS, t0.LAB_UNITS, t0.TOTAL_UNITS, t0.GRADE_TYPE, t0.GRADE_RULE, min(t0.TOTAL_UNITS) OVER (PARTITION BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE) AS min_total_units_by_dept FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN CIS_COURSE_CATALOG t1 ON t0.SUBJECT_ID = t1.SUBJECT_ID WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ORDER BY t0.DEPARTMENT_CODE

question: For each department and subject code in the Political Science department where the responsible faculty member's office is not null, provide the number of unique subjects and the minimum office phone number of the responsible faculty member. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE, COUNT(DISTINCT c.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(e.OFFICE_PHONE) AS min_office_phone FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN EMPLOYEE_DIRECTORY e ON c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = e.MIT_ID WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' AND e.OFFICE_LOCATION IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, c.SUBJECT_CODE ;

question: For each HGN code in the Political Science department, what is the department name, the maximum number of lecture units among all subjects in the course catalog, and the subject title from the subject offered table, for subjects offered in the year 2012 with more than 2 lecture units? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.HGN_CODE, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, MAX(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS max_lecture_units, s.SUBJECT_TITLE FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED s ON c.HGN_CODE = s.HGN_CODE WHERE c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2012 AND c.LECTURE_UNITS > 2 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Political Science' GROUP BY c.HGN_CODE, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, s.SUBJECT_TITLE HAVING MAX(c.LECTURE_UNITS) > 2;

question: For all subjects offered in the academic year 2022 by the Mathematics department that have at least one associated TIP material, show the subject ID, subject title, term code, term description, and the rank of each subject within its term (ordered by subject ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.SUBJECT_ID, c.SUBJECT_TITLE, c.TERM_CODE, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.TERM_CODE ORDER BY c.SUBJECT_ID) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c INNER JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE INNER JOIN TIP_DETAIL t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE AND c.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID WHERE c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year with a total of at least 6 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject code, subject number, department name, and the running sum of subject codes within each department, ordered by subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t2.SUBJECT_CODE, t2.SUBJECT_NUMBER, t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(t2.SUBJECT_CODE) OVER (PARTITION BY t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME ORDER BY t2.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t2 ON t1.TERM_CODE = t2.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE t2.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND t2.TOTAL_UNITS >= 6 AND t2.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For each academic year, give the academic year description and calculate the total number of units for all subjects offered in terms with a term status of 'Previous', where the total number of units is greater than 100, and only include subjects offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, SUM(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS total_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ata.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE at.TERM_STATUS = 'Previous' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC HAVING SUM(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 100;

question: For each department, give the department name and calculate the total number of enrolled students in subjects offered during terms that are not the current term, where the department is Mathematics (Course 18), and where the total number of enrolled students is greater than 10. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS total_enrolled FROM LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED lso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON lso.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs ON ata.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID WHERE ata.IS_CURRENT_TERM = 'N' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME HAVING SUM(lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) > 10;

question: For each academic year, what is the maximum number of total units for any subject offered in that year, and what is the corresponding term description, only considering subjects offered by the Mathematics department (Course 18) and only including academic years where the maximum total units is greater than 9? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH max_units_per_year AS ( SELECT c.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY c.ACADEMIC_YEAR HAVING max_total_units > 9 ) SELECT muy.ACADEMIC_YEAR, muy.max_total_units, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION FROM max_units_per_year muy JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c ON c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = muy.ACADEMIC_YEAR AND c.TOTAL_UNITS = muy.max_total_units AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON ata.TERM_CODE = c.TERM_CODE ORDER BY muy.ACADEMIC_YEAR;

question: For subjects offered in the academic year 2022 with a total of 12 units in the Mathematics department (Course 18), show the subject title, department name, department full name, offer school name, and the average number of enrolled students in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows grouped by the HGN code, ordered by the subject title. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.SUBJECT_TITLE, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, d.DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME, s.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, AVG(s.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.HGN_CODE ORDER BY c.SUBJECT_TITLE ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS avg_num_enrolled_students_window FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN SIS_DEPARTMENT d ON c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = d.DEPARTMENT_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY s ON d.DEPARTMENT_CODE = s.OFFER_DEPT_CODE AND c.SUBJECT_ID = s.SUBJECT_ID WHERE c.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND c.TOTAL_UNITS = 12 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ORDER BY c.SUBJECT_TITLE ;

question: What are the top 10 material statuses by the number of materials for courses in the Biology department, including the material status description and the count of materials for each status, considering only courses with materials? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS material_status_description, COUNT(td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS material_count FROM TIP_DETAIL td JOIN TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS tms ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON td.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID AND td.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Biology' AND (td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY IS NOT NULL AND td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY NOT LIKE 'N/ACourse has no materials%') GROUP BY tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS ORDER BY material_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: List the top 10 IAP activities by the number of subjects offered in the same academic term, showing the IAP activity title and the count of distinct subject titles offered in that term, for activities that are not cancelled, are offered in a term that is not the summer term, and where the subjects are from the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE, COUNT(DISTINCT ccs.SUBJECT_TITLE) AS subject_count FROM IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL iap JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata ON iap.TERM_CODE = ata.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs ON ata.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE WHERE iap.IS_CANCELLED = 'N' AND ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION NOT LIKE '%Summer%' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE ORDER BY subject_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: List the top 10 academic years by the number of subjects offered in the fall term by the Mathematics department, including the academic year description and the term description. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, COUNT(DISTINCT c.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON at.TERM_CODE = c.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND c.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY num_subjects DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each subject offered in the 2022 academic year by the Mathematics department, what is the maximum number of enrolled students for that subject, and what is the term description in which this maximum occurred, considering only subjects where the maximum enrollment is greater than 10? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.SUBJECT_TITLE, MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS max_enrollment, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON a.TERM_CODE = t.TERM_CODE AND c.SUBJECT_ID = t.SUBJECT_ID WHERE a.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_TITLE, a.TERM_DESCRIPTION HAVING MAX(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) > 10;

question: For each academic year, what is the highest total units among all subjects offered in that year from the Mathematics department, and what is the term description for the corresponding term, considering only subjects that are offered this year and have more than 6 total units? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, MAX(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS max_total_units, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS at JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE ccso.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y' AND ccso.TOTAL_UNITS > 6 AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION HAVING MAX(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) > 6;

question: For each academic term in 2022, list the term code, term description, and the number of subjects offered along with the total lecture units for subjects that are offered in the fall term, have at least 3 lecture units, and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT ata.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION, COUNT(DISTINCT cso.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_subjects_offered, SUM(cso.LECTURE_UNITS) AS total_lecture_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso ON ata.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE WHERE ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2022 AND cso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND cso.LECTURE_UNITS >= 3 AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ata.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY ata.TERM_CODE ;

question: For all rooms with an area greater than 400 in the Stata building, show the room key, building room, area, the subject title of the course meeting in that room that is offered by the Computer Science department, the academic year, and the rank of each room within its building (ordered by room key). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, t0.BUILDING_ROOM, t0.AREA, t1.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.ACADEMIC_YEAR, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t0.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY ORDER BY t0.FCLT_ROOM_KEY) AS window_column FROM FCLT_ROOMS t0 JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t1 ON t0.FCLT_ROOM_KEY = t1.MEET_PLACE WHERE t0.AREA > 400 AND t0.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = 32 AND t1.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci'

question: For each subject, give the subject ID, the minimum number of enrolled students and the average lecture units for each subject in the Mathematics department, for subjects where the number of enrolled students is between 2 and 10 or the academic year is at least 2020, and the term start date is between '01-JAN-20' and '31-DEC-22'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.SUBJECT_ID, MIN(t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) AS min_num_enrolled_students, AVG(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS avg_lecture_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL a ON c.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE JOIN TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED t ON t.TERM_CODE = a.TERM_CODE AND t.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ( (t.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS BETWEEN 2 AND 10) OR (a.ACADEMIC_YEAR >= 2020) ) AND a.TERM_START_DATE BETWEEN '01-JAN-20' AND '31-DEC-22' GROUP BY c.SUBJECT_ID;

question: For each IAP activity offered in the 2021 January term that is associated with at least one subject with more than 3 lecture units and offered by the Mathematics department, what is the maximum number of lecture units among its associated catalog subjects, along with the activity title and the term description? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, MAX(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) AS max_lecture_units FROM IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL iap JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON iap.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE WHERE iap.TERM_CODE = '2021JA' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY iap.ACTIVITY_TITLE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION HAVING MAX(ccso.LECTURE_UNITS) > 3;

question: For each subject offered by the library in the term "2014FA" with more than 5 enrolled students and offered by the Mathematics department, show the subject ID, subject title, the term description, the department name from the course catalog, and the running sum of enrolled students within each offer department code group ordered by subject ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT lso.SUBJECT_ID, lso.SUBJECT_TITLE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION, cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, SUM(lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS) OVER (PARTITION BY lso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE ORDER BY lso.SUBJECT_ID) AS running_sum_enrolled_students FROM LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED lso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON lso.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso ON lso.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID AND lso.TERM_CODE = cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE WHERE lso.TERM_CODE = '2014FA' AND lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS > 5 AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' ORDER BY lso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, lso.SUBJECT_ID;

question: List the top 10 department names and their corresponding academic years with the highest number of subjects offered, considering only subjects that are offered in the fall term and are from the Mathematics department (Course 18). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(so.SUBJECT_KEY) AS subject_count FROM SUBJECT_OFFERED so JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON so.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccs ON at.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE WHERE ccs.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR ORDER BY subject_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For all subjects offered in the academic year 2024 by the Mathematics department, show the subject code, subject title, term description, and the rank of each subject within its term description group ordered by subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT t0.SUBJECT_CODE, t0.SUBJECT_TITLE, t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY t1.TERM_DESCRIPTION ORDER BY t0.SUBJECT_CODE) AS window_column FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED t0 JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS t1 ON t0.TERM_CODE = t1.TERM_CODE WHERE t0.ACADEMIC_YEAR = 2024 AND t0.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics'

question: For all course subjects in the catalog where the department code is 18 (Mathematics), the department name is 'Mathematics', and the subject is offered this year, show the subject code, subject number, department name, responsible faculty's full name, Moira list member, and the average office phone number in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows grouped by the responsible faculty's last name and ordered by the subject code. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT c.SUBJECT_CODE, c.SUBJECT_NUMBER, c.DEPARTMENT_NAME, ed.FULL_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_FULL_NAME, mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER, AVG(ed.OFFICE_PHONE) OVER ( PARTITION BY ed.LAST_NAME ORDER BY c.SUBJECT_CODE ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS AVG_OFFICE_PHONE_WINDOW FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c JOIN EMPLOYEE_DIRECTORY ed ON c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = ed.MIT_ID LEFT JOIN MOIRA_LIST_DETAIL mld ON ed.MIT_ID = mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID WHERE c.DEPARTMENT_CODE = 18 AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND c.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y' ORDER BY c.SUBJECT_CODE ;

question: Which three academic terms had the highest number of subjects offered by the Mathematics department, and for each, what is the term code, the term description, and the academic year description? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT ata.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL ata JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON ata.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso ON at.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE WHERE cso.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y' AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' GROUP BY ata.TERM_CODE, ata.TERM_DESCRIPTION, ata.ACADEMIC_YEAR_DESC ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3;

question: For each department and academic year where the subject enrollment number is greater than 10 and the department is Mathematics, provide the number of unique subjects and the minimum total units offered. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR, COUNT(DISTINCT ss.SUBJECT_ID) AS num_unique_subjects, MIN(ss.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED cso JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN SUBJECT_SUMMARY ss ON at.TERM_CODE = ss.TERM_CODE AND cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = ss.DEPARTMENT_NAME WHERE cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics' AND ss.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER > 10 GROUP BY cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME, at.ACADEMIC_YEAR

question: What is the minimum total units and the sum of lecture units for subjects offered in the Spring Term 2021 that are letter graded and are in the Mathematics department (Course 18)? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT MIN(c.TOTAL_UNITS) AS min_total_units, SUM(c.LECTURE_UNITS) AS sum_lecture_units FROM ACADEMIC_TERMS_ALL a JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED c ON a.TERM_CODE = c.TERM_CODE WHERE a.TERM_CODE = '2021SP' AND c.GRADE_TYPE = 'L' AND c.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics';

question: What is the minimum academic year and the sum of total units for subjects that are offered in the fall term and belong to the Mathematics department, considering only library reserve material details with material status 'U'? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT MIN(at.ACADEMIC_YEAR) AS min_academic_year, SUM(ccso.TOTAL_UNITS) AS sum_total_units FROM LIBRARY_RESERVE_MATRL_DETAIL lrd JOIN ACADEMIC_TERMS at ON lrd.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE JOIN COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED ccso ON at.TERM_CODE = ccso.TERM_CODE AND lrd.SUBJECT_ID = ccso.SUBJECT_ID WHERE lrd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = 'U' AND ccso.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM = 'Y' AND ccso.DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Mathematics';

question: List the unique full room names, their corresponding building names, street addresses, cities, states, postal codes, and building heights for rooms associated with subjects that Computer Science students can enroll in.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME, b.BUILDING_NAME, b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS, fba.CITY, fba.STATE, fba.POSTAL_CODE, fb.BUILDING_HEIGHT FROM COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED JOIN FCLT_ROOMS fr ON MEET_PLACE = FCLT_ROOM_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING_ADDRESS fba ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN FCLT_BUILDING fb ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY JOIN BUILDINGS b ON b.BUILDING_KEY = fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY WHERE DEPARTMENT_NAME = 'Electrical Eng & Computer Sci' AND fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET';

question: For tenants that are in the top 10 by distinct DOWN ports and also in the top 10 by IPv4 subnet count, return the tenant ID, total distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have an IP allocation, total IPv4 subnets, and whether any IPv4 subnet has a standard attribute record with a non-null updated-at timestamp—keeping only tenants where DOWN ports are more than 75% of their IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.ip_address) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ip_allocations FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), ipv4_subnets_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT s.ID) AS total_ipv4_subnets, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT sa.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_updated_standard_attribute FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.NAME = s.NAME WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND sa.UPDATED_AT IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ipv4_subnets DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT d.tenant_id, d.total_down_ports, d.has_ip_allocations, i.total_ipv4_subnets, i.has_any_updated_standard_attribute FROM down_ports_by_tenant d JOIN ipv4_subnets_by_tenant i ON d.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE (d.total_down_ports * 1.0 / i.total_ipv4_subnets) > 0.75 ORDER BY (d.total_down_ports * 1.0 / i.total_ipv4_subnets) DESC, d.total_down_ports DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and that also have a standard attribute ID above the average for their resource type, list each port’s port ID and tenant ID along with host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-address-ordered row number (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count benchmark and the tenant usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), plus the port’s MAC address and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within its resource type. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH DownPortTenantUsage AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp), DownPortStandardAttrWindow AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE)), CombinedDownPorts AS ( SELECT u.port_id, u.tenant_id, u.host, u.vif_type, u.ip_address, u.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, u.total_down_ports, u.benchmark, u.user_category, s.mac_address, s.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum FROM DownPortTenantUsage u JOIN DownPortStandardAttrWindow s ON s.port_id = u.port_id AND s.tenant_id = u.tenant_id ) SELECT * FROM CombinedDownPorts ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, plus the port’s MAC address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the security group’s total number of DOWN ports, and that security group’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, q1.total_down_ports AS total_down_ports_for_tenant, q1.avg_down_port_count AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants, q2.mac_address, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q1.ip_address, q1.port_id;

question: For ports that are in status 'DOWN', list each port’s tenant ID and port ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also show, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average host total, and for the same tenant include the tenant’s count of DOWN ports with port security enabled, the overall average of that count across tenants as a benchmark, the tenant’s user category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.tenant_id, q2.user_category, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_secure_ports_benchmark, q2.overall_down_secure_ports, q1.port_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.tenant_id = q2.TENANT_ID ORDER BY q2.user_category, q1.tenant_id, q1.ip_address;

question: For ports that are in status 'DOWN', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID). Also show the total number of DOWN ports in that security group and how far that group’s DOWN-port count deviates from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups; additionally, for the same tenant, include how many DOWN ports have port security enabled, that tenant’s deviation from the average tenant count, and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), TenantDownSecurePorts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AverageTenantCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts) SELECT tdsp.tenant_id, tdsp.down_secure_ports, (tdsp.down_secure_ports - atc.avg_down_secure_ports) AS deviation_from_avg, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCounts atc CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_ports_in_group, q1.deviation_from_avg_down_ports, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.deviation_from_avg, q2.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.tenant_id = q1.tenant_id;

question: For networks that are ACTIVE, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard attribute updated_at timestamp (with a row number within each tenant ordered by network name), along with the benchmark average MTU across all active networks and an MTU category (ABOVE_AVG_MTU/BELOW_AVG_MTU/AT_AVG_MTU); for those same networks, also list any ports that are DOWN on the network including port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within each network ordered by port ID, the total number of DOWN port IP allocations on that network, and that total’s deviation from the average across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda ), active_networks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id AS network_tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, an.benchmark_avg_mtu, an.mtu_category, dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id AS port_tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column AS port_row_number_within_network, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg AS deviation_from_avg_down_allocated_ips FROM active_networks an JOIN down_ports dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id;

question: For the top 3 networks with the most subnets among RBAC entries where the action is 'access_as_shared', show each network (with its subnet count) and each subnet’s tenant ID, along with (on those same networks) the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID for DOWN ports in the same resource type, and the average of their running-sum standard attribute ID window values. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_windowed AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE) ), top_shared_network_subnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.network_id) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id) = inner_cte.network_id THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.network_id END AS network_id, inner_cte.subnet_count, s.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id FROM inner_cte JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = inner_cte.network_id ORDER BY inner_cte.network_id, s.TENANT_ID ), down_ports_on_top_shared_networks AS ( SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.mac_address, dpw.window_column, tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count, tsn.subnet_tenant_id FROM down_ports_windowed dpw JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dpw.port_id JOIN top_shared_network_subnets tsn ON tsn.network_id = p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dptsn.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(dptsn.window_column) AS avg_down_port_running_sum_standard_attr_ids FROM down_ports_on_top_shared_networks dptsn GROUP BY dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_count, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id ORDER BY dptsn.subnet_count DESC, dptsn.network_id, dptsn.subnet_tenant_id;

question: List the tenant ID for tenants who are either in the top 10 by number of DOWN ports or in the top 10 by number of non-default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0), showing the reason for inclusion, the corresponding count (DOWN ports or non-default external networks), and a Yes/No flag indicating whether they have any DOWN ports with standard attribute resource type 'ports' or (for non-default external networks) whether any of those networks have at least one RBAC entry. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortTenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT sa2.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ports_resource_type FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id LEFT JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID AND sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), NonDefaultExternalNetworkTenants AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ) SELECT n.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT n.ID) AS total_nondefault_external_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT r.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_rbac FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID LEFT JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID JOIN inner_cte ic ON ic.NAME = n.NAME WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 GROUP BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_nondefault_external_networks DESC LIMIT 10 ), CombinedTopTenants AS ( SELECT dpt.tenant_id AS tenant_id, 'Top DOWN Ports' AS reason, dpt.total_down_ports AS metric_count, dpt.has_ports_resource_type AS flag FROM DownPortTenants dpt UNION ALL SELECT ndent.tenant_id AS tenant_id, 'Top Non-default External Networks' AS reason, ndent.total_nondefault_external_networks AS metric_count, ndent.has_any_rbac AS flag FROM NonDefaultExternalNetworkTenants ndent ) SELECT tenant_id, reason, metric_count, flag FROM CombinedTopTenants ORDER BY tenant_id, reason;

question: How many distinct tenants have DOWN ports with IP allocations, and among those tenants how many are categorized as HIGH_USER based on having at least 50% more DOWN ports than the average across tenants with DOWN ports? Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH down_port_ip_details AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), tenant_down_port_benchmark AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT dpipd.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_down_port_ip_allocations, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tdpb.user_category = 'HIGH_USER' THEN tdpb.tenant_id END) AS high_user_tenants_among_down_port_tenants FROM down_port_ip_details dpipd JOIN tenant_down_port_benchmark tdpb ON dpipd.tenant_id = tdpb.tenant_id;

question: For the top 10 tenants with ports in DOWN status, show each tenant ID, the total number of distinct DOWN ports, whether any of those DOWN ports have at least one IP allocation, the total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled, and the average DOWN-and-port-secure port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_ipallocs AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.ip_address) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ip_allocations FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), down_secure_ports_by_tenant AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ) SELECT p.tenant_id AS ports_tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_secure_port_count FROM ( SELECT p2.tenant_id, COUNT(p2.id) AS port_count FROM ports p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings psb2 ON p2.id = psb2.port_id WHERE p2.status = 'DOWN' AND psb2.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p2.tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 CROSS JOIN inner_cte WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id, avg_counts.avg_down_secure_port_count ) SELECT dpi.tenant_id, dpi.total_down_ports, dpi.has_ip_allocations, dsp.total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, dsp.avg_down_secure_port_count FROM down_ports_ipallocs dpi JOIN down_secure_ports_by_tenant dsp ON dsp.ports_tenant_id = dpi.tenant_id ORDER BY dpi.total_down_ports DESC;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN', show each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, plus the port’s MAC address, the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the security group’s total number of DOWN ports, and that group’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, q1.total_down_ports AS tenant_total_down_ports, q1.avg_down_port_count AS avg_down_ports_per_tenant, q2.mac_address, q2.window_column AS security_group_running_sum_standard_attr_id, q2.down_ports_in_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q1.ip_address;

question: For ports with status DOWN, which ports (matched by MAC address, host, and VIF type) appear in both (1) the IP-address-ordered row-number window output that also includes each tenant’s total DOWN-port count and the average DOWN-port count across tenants, and (2) the VIF-type-partitioned admin_state_up window-average output where the window average is above the overall average for that VIF type? Return the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the IP-based window row number, the tenant’s total DOWN ports, the overall average DOWN-port count, plus the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up, and the admin_state_up window average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_ip_window AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.host, inner_cte.vif_type, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down ON 1 = 1 ), down_ports_admin_window_filtered AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeAverages v ON i.VIF_TYPE = v.VIF_TYPE WHERE i.window_column > v.avg_window_column ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT dipw.port_id, dipw.tenant_id, dipw.host, dipw.vif_type, dipw.ip_address, dipw.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, dipw.total_down_ports, dipw.avg_down_port_count, dapwf.NAME AS port_name, dapwf.MAC_ADDRESS, dapwf.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dapwf.window_column AS admin_state_up_window_avg FROM down_ports_ip_window dipw JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dipw.port_id JOIN down_ports_admin_window_filtered dapwf ON dapwf.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS AND dapwf.HOST = dipw.host AND dapwf.VIF_TYPE = dipw.vif_type;

question: For ACTIVE networks, show the network ID, network name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the standard attribute updated_at timestamp, the row number within each tenant ordered by network name, the overall average MTU across all ACTIVE networks (as a benchmark), and an MTU category (ABOVE_AVG_MTU/BELOW_AVG_MTU/AT_AVG_MTU); additionally, only include networks that have DOWN ports whose 2-preceding/2-following window average of port admin_state_up (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address) is greater than the overall average of that window average for the same VIF type, and list those ports’ name, MAC address, admin_state_up, binding host, VIF type, and window average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeAverages v ON i.VIF_TYPE = v.VIF_TYPE WHERE i.window_column > v.avg_window_column ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ), q2_ports AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, q2.NAME AS port_name, q2.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, q2.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS port_admin_state_up, q2.HOST AS binding_host, q2.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, q2.window_column AS port_admin_state_up_window_avg FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = q2.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.NAME = q2.NAME WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT q1.network_id, q1.network_name, q1.tenant_id, q1.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up, q1.mtu, q1.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.window_column AS tenant_network_name_rownum, q1.benchmark_avg_mtu, q1.mtu_category, q2_ports.port_name, q2_ports.mac_address, q2_ports.port_admin_state_up, q2_ports.binding_host, q2_ports.vif_type, q2_ports.port_admin_state_up_window_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2_ports ON q1.network_id = q2_ports.network_id ORDER BY q1.tenant_id, q1.network_name, q2_ports.mac_address;

question: For ports that are DOWN and appear in both the ML2 port bindings and security-group bindings views, list each port’s ID, name, tenant ID, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, and VIF type; also include (1) the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows within each VIF type ordered by MAC address, along with the DOWN-port count per VIF type and its deviation from the overall average across VIF types, and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group plus the tenant’s total DOWN-port count, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), VifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AverageVifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_vif_type) AS avg_down_ports_per_vif_type FROM VifTypeCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column, vtc.down_ports_in_vif_type, (vtc.down_ports_in_vif_type - avc.avg_down_ports_per_vif_type) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeCounts vtc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vtc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN AverageVifTypeCounts avc ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageDownPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPorts tdp ON i.tenant_id = tdp.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts adp ) SELECT q2.port_id, q1.NAME AS port_name, q2.tenant_id, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q1.HOST AS binding_host, q1.VIF_TYPE, q1.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif, q1.down_ports_in_vif_type, q1.deviation_from_avg AS vif_type_down_port_count_deviation_from_avg, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.total_down_ports AS tenant_total_down_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants_benchmark, q2.user_category AS tenant_user_category FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.mac_address = q1.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY q1.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For ports in status 'DOWN', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also show, per host, the total number of DOWN-port IP allocations and each row’s deviation from the average DOWN-port IP allocations per host; and for the same tenant, include the tenant’s count of DOWN ports with port security enabled, the average of that count across tenants as a benchmark, the tenant’s usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER), and the overall total number of DOWN ports with port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers. Classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.host, q1.vif_type, q1.ip_address, q1.window_column, q1.down_allocated_ips, q1.deviation_from_avg, q2.down_secure_ports, q2.benchmark AS avg_down_secure_ports_benchmark, q2.user_category, q2.overall_down_secure_ports FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q1.host, q1.ip_address;
