question: For DOWN ports that belong to ACTIVE networks, list each port’s ID, port tenant ID, port name, network ID, network name, network tenant ID, admin_state_up, MTU, the network standard attribute updated_at timestamp, the row number of the network within its tenant (ordered by network name), the average MTU across all active networks and the network’s MTU category versus that average, plus the port MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number of the port within its network (ordered by port ID), and for that network the total number of DOWN port IP allocations and the deviation of that total from the average across all networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), NetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id ), AverageNetworkDownAllocations AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM NetworkDownAllocations ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.window_column, nda.down_allocated_ips, (nda.down_allocated_ips - anda.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownAllocations nda ON i.network_id = nda.network_id CROSS JOIN AverageNetworkDownAllocations anda ), active_networks AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), AvgMtu AS (SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.window_column, a.avg_mtu AS benchmark_avg_mtu, CASE WHEN i.mtu > a.avg_mtu THEN 'ABOVE_AVG_MTU' WHEN i.mtu < a.avg_mtu THEN 'BELOW_AVG_MTU' ELSE 'AT_AVG_MTU' END AS mtu_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgMtu a ) SELECT dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id AS port_tenant_id, dp.port_name, dp.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id AS network_tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_rownum_within_tenant, an.benchmark_avg_mtu, an.mtu_category, dp.mac_address, dp.device_owner, dp.ip_address, dp.window_column AS port_rownum_within_network, dp.down_allocated_ips, dp.deviation_from_avg FROM down_ports dp JOIN active_networks an ON dp.network_id = an.network_id;

question: For DOWN ports on network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d` that are bound to a security group, show the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows (ordered by port ID), along with (per device owner) the total number of such ports and the average of these totals across device owners; additionally, only include device owners whose DOWN ports (bound to a security group) for tenant `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7` have a distinct port count greater than the average across all (status, device owner) groups, and for those owners also display that distinct port count and the minimum standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.NETWORK_ID, inner_cte.MAC_ADDRESS, inner_cte.ADMIN_STATE_UP, inner_cte.STATUS, inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER, inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.window_column, owner_stats.total_ports_per_owner, avg_owner_stats.avg_ports_per_owner FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT DEVICE_OWNER, COUNT(*) AS total_ports_per_owner FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEVICE_OWNER ) AS owner_stats ON inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER = owner_stats.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_ports_per_owner FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEVICE_OWNER ) AS sub ) AS avg_owner_stats ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.port_count > (SELECT avg_port_count FROM avg_cte) ) SELECT q1.NAME, q1.NETWORK_ID, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q1.STATUS, q1.DEVICE_OWNER, q1.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, q1.window_column, q1.total_ports_per_owner, q1.avg_ports_per_owner, q2.port_count, q2.min_standard_attr_id FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.STATUS = q2.port_status AND q1.DEVICE_OWNER = q2.device_owner;

question: For DOWN ports on network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d` and DOWN ports for tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, matched by MAC address, return the network ID and tenant ID along with: the number of matched DOWN-port rows, the average deviation of each port’s windowed minimum `admin_state_up` from the overall average of that windowed minimum, the average running sum of `standard_attr_id` within each security group, the total number of DOWN ports for that tenant, and the average number of DOWN ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), avg_window AS (SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.NAME, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.window_column, (i.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_window_min FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_window a ), subq2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports_for_tenant, avg_counts.avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM inner_cte JOIN (SELECT p.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_for_tenant FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM (SELECT COUNT(p.id) AS port_count FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id) AS sub) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT subq1.NETWORK_ID, subq2.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS joined_down_port_rows, AVG(subq1.deviation_from_avg_window_min) AS avg_deviation_from_avg_window_min, AVG(subq2.window_column) AS avg_running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_sg, MAX(subq2.total_down_ports_for_tenant) AS total_down_ports_for_tenant, MAX(subq2.avg_down_ports_across_tenants) AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.MAC_ADDRESS = subq2.mac_address GROUP BY subq1.NETWORK_ID, subq2.tenant_id;

question: For ports that are bound to a security group with status = 'DOWN' and tenant ID in ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'), list each (port status, device owner) group with its distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, the overall average distinct-port count across all such groups, and the benchmark-based category (HIGH_GROUP / LOW_GROUP / AVERAGE_GROUP). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each group as 'HIGH_GROUP' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_GROUP' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_GROUP'.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ), subq2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.port_status, ic.device_owner, ic.port_count, ic.min_standard_attr_id, ac.avg_port_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.port_count > ac.avg_port_count * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_GROUP' WHEN ic.port_count < ac.avg_port_count * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_GROUP' ELSE 'AVERAGE_GROUP' END AS group_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN avg_cte ac ) SELECT s1.port_status, s1.device_owner, s1.port_count AS distinct_port_count, s1.min_standard_attr_id, s1.avg_port_count AS overall_avg_distinct_port_count, s2.benchmark AS overall_avg_port_count_benchmark, s2.group_category FROM subq1 s1 JOIN subq2 s2 ON s1.port_status = s2.port_status AND s1.device_owner = s2.device_owner AND s1.port_count = s2.port_count AND s1.min_standard_attr_id = s2.min_standard_attr_id;

question: For tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7' and port status 'DOWN', list the top 10 device owners (with security-group-bound ports) showing their distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, whether any of their ports have multiple security group bindings, the maximum number of ports owned by any single device owner for that same port status among non-shared networks with standard attribute resource type 'ports', and the normalized ratio (device owner distinct port count divided by that per-status maximum).
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT port_status, MAX(port_count) AS max_ports_for_any_device_owner FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT spb2.security_group_id) > COUNT(DISTINCT p2.id) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_multi_sg_bindings FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p2 ON p2.status = i.port_status AND p2.device_owner = i.device_owner AND p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') JOIN securitygroupportbindings spb2 ON p2.id = spb2.port_id GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT q2.port_status, q2.device_owner, q2.port_count AS distinct_port_count, q2.min_standard_attr_id, q2.has_multi_sg_bindings, q1.max_ports_for_any_device_owner, ROUND(q2.port_count / NULLIF(q1.max_ports_for_any_device_owner, 0), 2) AS normalized_device_owner_port_count_ratio FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.port_status = q2.port_status ORDER BY normalized_device_owner_port_count_ratio DESC, q2.port_count DESC;

question: For ports that are in status DOWN on network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, return the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin_state_up, status, device owner, and bound security group ID, along with (1) the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by port ID, (2) the total number of such DOWN ports per device owner and the average of these totals across device owners, and (3) for the same network (as computed from tenant `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`), the count of DOWN ports with port security enabled and that count’s deviation from the average across the tenant’s networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.NETWORK_ID, inner_cte.MAC_ADDRESS, inner_cte.ADMIN_STATE_UP, inner_cte.STATUS, inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER, inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.window_column, owner_stats.total_ports_per_owner, avg_owner_stats.avg_ports_per_owner FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT DEVICE_OWNER, COUNT(*) AS total_ports_per_owner FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEVICE_OWNER ) AS owner_stats ON inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER = owner_stats.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_ports_per_owner FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY DEVICE_OWNER ) AS sub ) AS avg_owner_stats ON 1 = 1 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7')), NetworkCounts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ), AverageCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_with_port_security_enabled) AS avg_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM NetworkCounts ) SELECT nc.network_id, nc.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, (nc.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled - ac.avg_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled) AS deviation_from_avg FROM NetworkCounts nc CROSS JOIN AverageCounts ac ) SELECT q1.NAME, q1.NETWORK_ID, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q1.STATUS, q1.DEVICE_OWNER, q1.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, q1.window_column, q1.total_ports_per_owner, q1.avg_ports_per_owner, q2.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled, q2.deviation_from_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.NETWORK_ID = q2.network_id;

question: For DOWN ports belonging to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and its rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), while also showing for the port’s security group the total number of such DOWN ports, the average (benchmark) across security groups, and the security group’s usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not repeat the security group ID on consecutive rows when ordering by security group ID then port ID. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each security group as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(security_group_id) OVER (ORDER BY security_group_id, port_id) = security_group_id THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group FROM inner_cte ORDER BY security_group_id, port_id ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), SecurityGroupPorts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM SecurityGroupPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, sgp.total_ports AS total_down_ports_in_security_group, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN sgp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN sgp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN SecurityGroupPorts sgp ON i.security_group_id = sgp.security_group_id CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap ) SELECT q2.security_group_id, q2.total_down_ports_in_security_group, q2.benchmark, q2.user_category, q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.port_rank_within_security_group FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.port_id = q1.port_id ORDER BY q2.security_group_id, q1.port_id;

question: For DOWN ports belonging to tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, for each security group, how many distinct ports have a running sum of the port standard attribute ID (within that security group) that is both greater than 100 and greater than the overall average running sum across all such ports, and what is the average of that running sum for those ports? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte) ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON inner_cte.port_id = sgpb.PORT_ID WHERE inner_cte.window_column > 100 ORDER BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.window_column ) SELECT q2.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT q2.port_id) AS ports_meeting_both_thresholds, AVG(q2.window_column) AS avg_running_sum_for_these_ports FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.port_id = q1.port_id AND q2.tenant_id = q1.tenant_id AND q2.mac_address = q1.mac_address AND q2.window_column = q1.window_column GROUP BY q2.security_group_id ORDER BY ports_meeting_both_thresholds DESC, q2.security_group_id;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each ACTIVE network (network ID, name, admin_state_up, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at, plus the row number within the tenant by network name, the total active-network count for the tenant, and the average active-network count across tenants) together with any DOWN ports on that network whose rank within their security group (ordered by port ID) is greater than the average such rank; include the port ID, MAC address, security group ID, and the port’s security-group rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH port_rank_cte AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, security_group_id, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte) ), active_networks_cte AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND n.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT inner_cte.network_id, inner_cte.network_name, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.admin_state_up, inner_cte.mtu, inner_cte.standard_attr_updated_at, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_active_networks, avg_counts.avg_active_networks FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(network_id) AS total_active_networks FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_counts ON tenant_counts.tenant_id = inner_cte.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(active_network_count) AS avg_active_networks FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(network_id) AS active_network_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, an.total_active_networks, an.avg_active_networks, pr.port_id, pr.mac_address, pr.security_group_id, pr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group FROM active_networks_cte an JOIN PORTS p ON p.tenant_id = an.tenant_id AND p.network_id = an.network_id AND p.status = 'DOWN' JOIN port_rank_cte pr ON pr.port_id = p.id AND pr.tenant_id = an.tenant_id ORDER BY an.total_active_networks DESC, an.network_name, pr.security_group_id, pr.port_id;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN' that belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', show each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and security group ID, along with (1) the port’s rank within its security group by port ID, (2) the total number of such DOWN ports in that security group, (3) the average of those totals across security groups as a benchmark, (4) a category per security group (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER) based on that benchmark, and also (5) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) plus (6) the deviation of the port’s standard attribute ID from the overall average standard attribute ID across these DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each security group as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), SecurityGroupPorts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ), AveragePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM SecurityGroupPorts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, sgp.total_ports AS total_down_ports_in_security_group, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN sgp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN sgp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN SecurityGroupPorts sgp ON i.security_group_id = sgp.security_group_id CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), AverageStdAttr AS (SELECT AVG(p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS p2 ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p2.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb2 ON p2.ID = psb2.PORT_ID WHERE p2.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p2.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, (p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID - a.avg_standard_attr_id) AS deviation_from_avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id CROSS JOIN AverageStdAttr a ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.security_group_id, q1.port_rank_within_security_group, q1.total_down_ports_in_security_group, q1.benchmark AS avg_down_ports_benchmark_across_security_groups, q1.user_category, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.deviation_from_avg_standard_attr_id FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id AND q1.mac_address = q2.mac_address;

question: For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the total number of DOWN ports they have (based on the DOWN ports joined to their security-group-to-port bindings and port-security bindings), and the average number of DOWN ports per tenant across all such tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT inner_cte.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_down_ports, avg_down.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ) AS avg_down GROUP BY inner_cte.tenant_id, avg_down.avg_down_port_count;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, for each host, the total number of such DOWN-port IP allocations and the deviation of each row from the average number of DOWN-port IP allocations per host. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostCounts AS ( SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_address) AS down_allocated_ips FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host ), AverageHostCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_allocated_ips) AS avg_down_allocated_ips FROM HostCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, hc.down_allocated_ips, (hc.down_allocated_ips - ahc.avg_down_allocated_ips) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i JOIN HostCounts hc ON i.host = hc.host CROSS JOIN AverageHostCounts ahc;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, but only include security groups that are bound to more than 5 DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT NAME, NETWORK_ID, MAC_ADDRESS, ADMIN_STATE_UP, STATUS, DEVICE_OWNER, SECURITY_GROUP_ID, window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE SECURITY_GROUP_ID IN (SELECT SECURITY_GROUP_ID FROM inner_cte GROUP BY SECURITY_GROUP_ID HAVING COUNT(*) > 5);

question: For networks that have more ports in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled than the average across all networks, list the network ID and the total number of such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), NetworkDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT network_id, total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts WHERE total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled > ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled) FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts );

question: For each tenant, report the number of ports that are in status 'DOWN' and have port security enabled, the average of that count across all tenants as a benchmark, and classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), TenantDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ), AverageDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts ) SELECT tdsp.TENANT_ID, tdsp.down_secure_ports, adsp.avg_down_secure_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports > adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdsp.down_secure_ports < adsp.avg_down_secure_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS overall_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageDownSecurePorts adsp CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID, but only include ports whose standard attribute ID is above the average standard attribute ID for DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = inner_cte.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT AVG(sa3.ID) FROM PORTS p3 JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa3 ON sa3.ID = p3.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p3.STATUS = 'DOWN');

question: For each security group, find the security group ID and the highest rank (when ordering DOWN ports by port ID within that security group) among all DOWN ports bound to that security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN') SELECT security_group_id, MAX(window_column) AS max_port_rank FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up in a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address; additionally, for each VIF type, include the total number of DOWN ports, the overall average of those per-VIF-type totals as a benchmark, and categorize each VIF type as 'HIGH_DOWN' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_DOWN' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_DOWN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), VifDownCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM VifDownCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column, vdc.total_down_ports, adc.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN vdc.total_down_ports > adc.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_DOWN' WHEN vdc.total_down_ports < adc.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_DOWN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_DOWN' END AS down_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifDownCounts vdc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vdc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts adc ORDER BY i.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the number of DOWN ports, the average number of DOWN ports across all such tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp;

question: For each tenant, how many ports are in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled, and what is the deviation of that count from the average across all tenants? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1), TenantDownSecurePorts AS (SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_secure_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID), AverageTenantCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_secure_ports) AS avg_down_secure_ports FROM TenantDownSecurePorts) SELECT tdsp.tenant_id, tdsp.down_secure_ports, (tdsp.down_secure_ports - atc.avg_down_secure_ports) AS deviation_from_avg, inner_cte.down_ports_with_port_security_enabled AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM TenantDownSecurePorts tdsp CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCounts atc CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; only include ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among DOWN ports for the same resource type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ResourceTypeAverages AS (SELECT sa.RESOURCE_TYPE, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.ID > (SELECT avg_standard_attr_id FROM ResourceTypeAverages rta WHERE rta.RESOURCE_TYPE = sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE);

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID, along with the overall average of these per-(status, owner) port counts across all such groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_counts;

question: List the top 10 port status and device owner combinations (restricted to DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), showing the distinct port count, the minimum standard attribute ID, and whether any of those ports appear in the security group port bindings table. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT spb2.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_security_group_bound_ports FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.STATUS = i.port_status AND p2.DEVICE_OWNER = i.device_owner LEFT JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb2 ON p2.ID = spb2.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Using the DOWN-port listing (port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row) as an inner result, return only the tenants whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per tenant, and show each qualifying tenant ID with its total DOWN-port count. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS total_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT tenant_id, total_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts WHERE total_down_ports > (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) FROM TenantDownPorts);

question: For each VIF type, find the VIF type and the highest windowed average of the admin_state_up flag (computed over 2 preceding and 2 following rows ordered by MAC address) among ports that are DOWN. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(window_column) AS max_windowed_avg_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE;

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only DOWN ports that are bound to a security group), return the port status, device owner, number of distinct ports, and minimum standard attribute ID, but only include those (status, owner) groups whose distinct port count is greater than the average distinct port count across all such groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT port_status, device_owner, port_count, min_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte WHERE port_count > (SELECT AVG(port_count) FROM inner_cte);

question: For hosts where more than 60% of their DOWN ports (with IP allocations) use the VIF type 'ovs', list the host name, total number of DOWN ports, number of DOWN ports using 'ovs', and the ovs share. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), HostVifShare AS (SELECT host, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_ports, SUM(CASE WHEN vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ovs_down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY host) SELECT host, down_ports, ovs_down_ports, (ovs_down_ports * 1.0 / down_ports) AS ovs_share FROM HostVifShare WHERE down_ports > 0 AND (ovs_down_ports * 1.0 / down_ports) > 0.60;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID). Also include, for each security group, the total number of DOWN ports and the deviation of that security group’s DOWN-port count from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), SecurityGroupDownCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ), AverageDownCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_in_group) AS avg_down_ports_in_group FROM SecurityGroupDownCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column, sgdc.down_ports_in_group, (sgdc.down_ports_in_group - adc.avg_down_ports_in_group) AS deviation_from_avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = i.port_id JOIN SecurityGroupDownCounts AS sgdc ON sgdc.security_group_id = sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID CROSS JOIN AverageDownCounts AS adc;

question: Using the set of ports whose status is DOWN and whose device ID is `da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7`, show each port’s tenant ID, the number of such ports the tenant has, the average number of such ports per tenant as a benchmark, and classify each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.device_id IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7')), TenantPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte JOIN ports AS p ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AveragePorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantPorts) SELECT tp.tenant_id, tp.total_ports, ap.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tp.total_ports > ap.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tp.total_ports < ap.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantPorts tp CROSS JOIN AveragePorts ap;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), along with the total number of such DOWN ports for that tenant and the average number of such DOWN ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.window_column, tenant_counts.total_down_ports_for_tenant, avg_counts.avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM inner_cte JOIN (SELECT p.tenant_id AS tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports_for_tenant FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id) AS tenant_counts ON inner_cte.tenant_id = tenant_counts.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM (SELECT COUNT(p.id) AS port_count FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id) AS sub) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group and whose tenant ID is '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID, along with the average distinct-port count across all such (status, device owner) groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: Using the per-(port status, device owner) results for ports that are bound to a security group and whose tenant ID is '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7' (with status restricted to 'DOWN'), list the top 10 device owners by distinct port count, showing the port status, device owner, distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, and whether any of those ports are associated with more than one security group binding. SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT spb2.security_group_id) > COUNT(DISTINCT p2.id) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_multi_sg_bindings FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p2 ON p2.status = i.port_status AND p2.device_owner = i.device_owner AND p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') JOIN securitygroupportbindings spb2 ON p2.id = spb2.port_id GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Using the set of ports that are DOWN and belong to network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d` (including their bound security group), for each tenant show the tenant ID, the number of such ports, the average number of such ports across all tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group and whose tenant ID is '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports that are bound to a security group and belong to tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', return the number of distinct ports and the minimum standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and whose device ID is `da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7`, list each port ID and the dense rank of that port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED), using a window frame that includes the current row and the 2 preceding rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.device_id IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7');

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and whose tenant ID is in ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'), show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7');

question: For the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list only the networks where more than 50% of the ports bound to that security group are in DOWN status, returning the network ID, total bound ports, total DOWN ports, and the DOWN-to-total ratio.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortNetwork AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT pn.network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id) AS total_ports_in_security_group, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) AS total_down_ports, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id), 0), 2 ) AS down_port_ratio FROM PortNetwork pn LEFT JOIN Subq1 s1 ON s1.port_id = pn.port_id LEFT JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s2.port_id = pn.port_id GROUP BY pn.network_id ) SELECT network_id, total_ports_in_security_group, total_down_ports, down_port_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE total_ports_in_security_group > 0 AND down_port_ratio > 0.50;

question: For each tenant, report the number of ports that are both DOWN (using a running sum of STANDARD_ATTR_ID within each security group) and administratively up (including port security binding counts and total enabled port security), show the average of this count across all tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), admin_up_ports_security AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count FROM down_ports_window dpw JOIN admin_up_ports_security aups ON dpw.port_id = aups.port_id AND dpw.tenant_id = aups.tenant_id AND dpw.mac_address = aups.mac_address), TenantDownAdminUpCounts AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_matching_ports FROM ports p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON psb.port_id = p.id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id ), AverageTenantCount AS ( SELECT AVG(total_matching_ports) AS avg_matching_ports FROM TenantDownAdminUpCounts ) SELECT t.tenant_id, t.total_matching_ports, a.avg_matching_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN t.total_matching_ports > a.avg_matching_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN t.total_matching_ports < a.avg_matching_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count AS overall_matching_ports_count FROM TenantDownAdminUpCounts t CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCount a CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For each VIF type among ports that are DOWN, list the VIF type, total number of distinct DOWN ports, the average of the MAC-address-based admin_state_up window metric, the maximum IP-address-based row-number window value, and the number of distinct tenants, but only return VIF types whose total number of distinct DOWN ports is greater than the average total number of distinct DOWN ports across all VIF types (computed from the same DOWN-port MAC/IP joined results). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortDownMacWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), PortDownIpRowNumber AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT p2.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.port_id) AS Total_Down_Ports, AVG(p1.window_column) AS Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, MAX(p2.window_column) AS Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.tenant_id) AS Distinct_Tenants FROM PortDownIpRowNumber p2 JOIN PortDownMacWindow p1 ON p1.HOST = p2.host AND p1.VIF_TYPE = p2.vif_type GROUP BY p2.vif_type ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC) SELECT vif_type, Total_Down_Ports, Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, Distinct_Tenants FROM inner_cte WHERE Total_Down_Ports > (SELECT AVG(Total_Down_Ports) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC;

question: Among the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports, show each tenant’s ID, total DOWN-port count, and whether they have any ports bound with VIF type 'ovs'. For each tenant, also include the tenant’s average admin_state_up for DOWN ports (rounded) and the maximum normalized VIF-type window average vs. the tenant average (computed from the DOWN-port details).
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), SecurityGroupPortRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPortSummary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(p.admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up_down FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT sgpr.tenant_id, tds.down_port_count, ROUND(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id, pbw.NAME AS port_name, sgpr.mac_address, pbw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, pbw.HOST AS binding_host, pbw.VIF_TYPE, pbw.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, sgpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, ROUND( pbw.window_column / NULLIF(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 0), 2 ) AS normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM SecurityGroupPortRank sgpr JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON pbw.MAC_ADDRESS = sgpr.mac_address JOIN TenantDownPortSummary tds ON tds.tenant_id = sgpr.tenant_id ORDER BY normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, ROUND(AVG(i.avg_admin_state_up_down), 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN i.vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_vif_type, MAX(i.normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg) AS max_normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each tenant that has at least one port which is admin_state_up = 1, bound to at least one security group, and has status DOWN, list the tenant ID, the number of such qualifying ports they have, and the average number of such qualifying ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SecurityGroupBoundPorts AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), DownPortBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT sgp.tenant_id, sgp.port_id, sgp.port_name, sgp.security_group_binding_count, sgp.dns_record_count, dpb.host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.ip_address, dpb.window_column FROM SecurityGroupBoundPorts sgp JOIN DownPortBindings dpb ON sgp.port_id = dpb.port_id WHERE sgp.security_group_binding_count >= 1 ORDER BY sgp.security_group_binding_count DESC, sgp.dns_record_count DESC, dpb.ip_address) SELECT i.tenant_id AS qualifying_ports_tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_qualifying_ports, avg_q.avg_qualifying_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(tenant_port_count) AS avg_qualifying_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS tenant_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS per_tenant ) AS avg_q ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY i.tenant_id, avg_q.avg_qualifying_port_count ORDER BY total_qualifying_ports DESC, qualifying_ports_tenant_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to ACTIVE networks, return the same port/network details as before (port ID, network ID, port name, MAC address, port admin_state_up, binding host, VIF type, the 2-preceding/2-following window average of port admin_state_up by VIF type ordered by MAC address; plus the active network’s name, tenant ID, network admin_state_up, MTU, the network standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the row number of the network within its tenant ordered by network name). Then, only keep rows where the network’s MTU is greater than the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), ActiveNetworksWithAttrs AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), DownPortsOnActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, dpb.NAME AS port_name, dpb.MAC_ADDRESS, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS port_admin_state_up, dpb.HOST AS binding_host, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpb.window_column AS port_admin_state_up_avg_window_2_pre_2_fol, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM PORTS p JOIN DownPortsWithBindings dpb ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = dpb.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.NAME = dpb.NAME AND p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP JOIN ActiveNetworksWithAttrs an ON an.network_id = p.NETWORK_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT * FROM DownPortsOnActiveNetworks ORDER BY tenant_id, network_id, MAC_ADDRESS ), ActiveNetworkMtuAvg AS ( SELECT AVG(n.MTU) AS avg_active_network_mtu FROM NETWORKS n WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT i.* FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN ActiveNetworkMtuAvg a WHERE i.mtu > a.avg_active_network_mtu ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For each tenant, find the tenant ID and the maximum number of security group bindings on any DOWN port (with admin_state_up = 1) for that tenant, considering only ports that have at least one security group binding, and also report the maximum total DNS records associated with any such port for that tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupAndDnsCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortBindingRanks AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpr.port_id, dpr.port_name, psc.tenant_id, dpr.mac_address, dpr.binding_host, dpr.vif_type, dpr.window_column AS down_status_rank, psc.security_group_binding_count, psc.dns_record_count FROM DownPortBindingRanks dpr JOIN PortSecurityGroupAndDnsCounts psc ON dpr.port_id = psc.port_id ORDER BY psc.security_group_binding_count DESC, psc.dns_record_count DESC, dpr.port_id ) SELECT tenant_id, MAX(security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_bindings_on_a_down_port, MAX(dns_record_count) AS max_dns_records_on_a_down_port FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id;

question: For tenants with at least 2 ports in DOWN status, return only those tenants whose number of distinct DOWN ports is greater than the average distinct DOWN-port count across all tenants; include the tenant ID, the distinct DOWN-port count, the minimum allocated IP address among those DOWN ports, and whether any of those DOWN ports have a bound security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsWithSecurityGroups AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpbip.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpbip.port_id) AS down_port_count, MIN(dpbip.ip_address) AS min_allocated_ip_address, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.SECURITY_GROUP_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Bound_Security_Groups FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs dpbip JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = dpbip.port_id JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityGroups dpsg ON dpsg.NETWORK_ID = p.NETWORK_ID AND dpsg.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpsg.STATUS = p.STATUS WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY dpbip.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dpbip.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, min_allocated_ip_address ASC) SELECT tenant_id, down_port_count, min_allocated_ip_address, Has_Bound_Security_Groups FROM inner_cte WHERE down_port_count > (SELECT AVG(down_port_count) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, min_allocated_ip_address ASC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, and security group ID, along with (1) the rank of the port within its security group when ordered by port ID and (2) the minimum admin_state_up value over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID; additionally, for each tenant include the total number of DOWN ports they have and the average number of DOWN ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_id, subq1.tenant_id, subq2.name AS port_name, subq2.network_id, subq1.mac_address, subq2.admin_state_up, subq2.status, subq2.device_owner, subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, subq2.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.security_group_id = subq2.security_group_id AND subq1.mac_address = subq2.mac_address ORDER BY subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column, subq1.port_id ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.tenant_id, inner_cte.port_name, inner_cte.network_id, inner_cte.mac_address, inner_cte.admin_state_up, inner_cte.status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.security_group_id, inner_cte.port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id, tenant_stats.total_down_ports, avg_stats.avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS tenant_stats ON tenant_stats.tenant_id = inner_cte.tenant_id JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports_across_tenants FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM PORTS WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS per_tenant ) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.security_group_id, inner_cte.port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, inner_cte.port_id;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, along with any DOWN ports on that network (port ID and MAC address), the port’s security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), and the network’s row number within its tenant (ordered by network name). Also include, for each row, the deviation of that network’s MTU from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT q2.network_id, q2.network_name, q2.tenant_id, q2.admin_state_up, q2.mtu, q2.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.port_id, q1.mac_address, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = q2.network_id JOIN q1 ON q1.port_id = p.id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q2.tenant_id, q2.network_name, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column, q1.port_id ), avg_active_mtu AS ( SELECT AVG(n.mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM NETWORKS n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.port_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.port_rank_within_security_group, i.network_row_number_within_tenant, (i.mtu - a.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_active_network_mtu FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_active_mtu a;

question: For each tenant that has at least 2 ports in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, the number of distinct DOWN ports, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (with a frame of the current row and 2 preceding rows). Also include the overall average DOWN-port count across all qualifying tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_DOWN' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'LOW_DOWN' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AVERAGE_DOWN'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id), Benchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window, b.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.down_port_count > b.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_DOWN' WHEN i.down_port_count < b.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_DOWN' ELSE 'AVERAGE_DOWN' END AS down_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN Benchmark b;

question: For active networks with admin_state_up = 1 that have at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports—only for those networks whose DOWN-port count is greater than the average DOWN-port count among all active admin_state_up = 1 networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name ) , DownPortAverages AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.network_name, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.down_port_count FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM DownPortAverages) ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.network_name;
