question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; additionally, for each tenant show the total number of distinct DOWN ports and the deviation of that tenant’s DOWN-port count from the average DOWN-port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address), TenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS down_ports FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageTenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPortCounts) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.standard_attr_running_sum_window, t.down_ports AS tenant_down_port_count, (t.down_ports - a.avg_down_ports) AS deviation_from_avg_tenant_down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPortCounts t ON t.tenant_id = i.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageTenantDownPortCounts a ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.port_id, i.ip_address;

question: From the top 10 tenants (among those with at least 2 DOWN ports) ranked by the number of distinct DOWN ports, show each tenant’s ID, the distinct DOWN port count, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (frame: 2 preceding to 1 following), the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (frame: 2 preceding to current row), and whether the tenant has any ports bound to a host (i.e., any ML2 port binding exists). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT b.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_port_binding FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.tenant_id = i.tenant_id LEFT JOIN ml2_port_bindings b ON b.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.tenant_id LIMIT 10;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return only those ports whose rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID) is greater than the average of those ranks across all DOWN ports; list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each standard attribute resource type (ordered by standard attribute ID), plus the port name, binding host, VIF type, and the port’s rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsStdAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT s.port_id, s.tenant_id, s.mac_address, s.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, b.port_name, b.binding_host, b.vif_type, b.window_column AS rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM DownPortsStdAttrWindow s JOIN DownPortsBindingRank b ON s.port_id = b.port_id AND s.mac_address = b.mac_address ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, port_name, binding_host, vif_type, rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM inner_cte WHERE rank_within_down_status_by_port_id > (SELECT AVG(rank_within_down_status_by_port_id) FROM inner_cte);

question: For each network that has at least one DOWN port bound to a security group, find the network ID and the maximum (across its ports) of the per-port row number computed by ordering allocated IP addresses with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, using the DOWN-port details and status/device-owner security-group summary as the inner result. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, MAX(i.window_column) AS max_ip_row_number FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID;

question: For each binding host, find the host name and the highest total number of times port security is enabled across any single port on that host—considering only ports that are DOWN but administratively up, and only including ports where port security is enabled at least once. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id), HostPortSecurity AS ( SELECT binding_host, port_id, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY binding_host, port_id ) SELECT binding_host, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS max_port_security_enabled_total FROM HostPortSecurity GROUP BY binding_host;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN', return only those ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among all DOWN ports with the same VIF type. For each such port, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, the port’s MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs d1 JOIN DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id AND d1.tenant_id = d2.tenant_id ), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_stdattr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.ID > (SELECT v.avg_stdattr_id FROM VifTypeAverages v WHERE v.vif_type = i.vif_type);

question: Using the DOWN-port details query as an inner CTE, list the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports. For each of these tenants, show the tenant ID, total number of DOWN ports, and whether any of their DOWN ports have an ML2 port binding with VIF type 'ovs'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortStandardAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpsaw.port_id, dpsaw.tenant_id, dpbr.port_name, dpsaw.mac_address, dpbr.binding_host, dpbr.vif_type, dpsaw.window_column AS standard_attr_id_running_sum_within_resource_type, dpbr.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM DownPortStandardAttrWindow dpsaw JOIN DownPortBindingRank dpbr ON dpsaw.port_id = dpbr.port_id AND dpsaw.mac_address = dpbr.mac_address ORDER BY dpsaw.port_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN i.vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_vif_type_on_any_down_port FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Using the DOWN-port result set from the existing query as an inner CTE, for each VIF type return the VIF type and the maximum number of distinct device owners observed among DOWN ports in that VIF type (where device owners come from the port-status/device-owner aggregation and VIF types come from the windowed DOWN-port set). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortsWindow dpw GROUP BY psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(distinct_device_owners) AS max_distinct_device_owners FROM (SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT device_owner) AS distinct_device_owners FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE) t GROUP BY VIF_TYPE;

question: For ports with status DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the corresponding summary for that port’s status and device owner considering only ports bound to a security group (distinct port count and minimum standard attribute ID), and add the average of these per-(status, device owner) port counts across all such DOWN groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, avg_counts.avg_port_count_across_down_status_owner_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count_across_down_status_owner_groups FROM ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) AS sub ) AS avg_counts ON 1 = 1;

question: For ports whose status is 'DOWN', list each port’s ID, name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and subnet ID, along with (1) the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type ordered by MAC address, and (2) the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address; additionally, for each VIF type show the total number of DOWN ports and the average of these DOWN-port counts across all VIF types. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH down_ports_bindings AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), down_ports_ipallocs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpi.port_id, dpi.port_name, dpi.mac_address, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpb.HOST, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpi.ip_address, dpi.subnet_id, dpb.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif_type, dpi.window_column AS avg_port_id_by_port_id_ordered_by_ip FROM down_ports_ipallocs dpi JOIN down_ports_bindings dpb ON dpi.port_name = dpb.NAME AND dpi.mac_address = dpb.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY dpi.ip_address ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol_by_vif_type, i.avg_port_id_by_port_id_ordered_by_ip, vif_stats.total_down_ports_for_vif_type, avg_vif_stats.avg_down_ports_across_vif_types FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ( SELECT vif_type, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_for_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type ) AS vif_stats ON i.vif_type = vif_stats.vif_type JOIN ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports_across_vif_types FROM ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY vif_type ) AS sub ) AS avg_vif_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For ports with status equal to 'DOWN', return the same port/IP details (port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID), but only for networks whose number of DOWN ports is greater than the average number of DOWN ports per network. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortIpWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), DownPortNetworkRowNum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpiw.port_id, dpnr.tenant_id, dpiw.port_name, dpnr.network_id, dpiw.mac_address, dpnr.device_owner, dpiw.ip_address, dpiw.subnet_id, dpiw.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, dpnr.window_column AS row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM DownPortIpWindow dpiw JOIN DownPortNetworkRowNum dpnr ON dpiw.port_id = dpnr.port_id AND dpiw.ip_address = dpnr.ip_address ORDER BY dpnr.network_id, dpnr.window_column, dpiw.ip_address ), NetworkDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.network_id, i.mac_address, i.device_owner, i.ip_address, i.subnet_id, i.avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, i.row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM inner_cte i JOIN NetworkDownPortCounts ndpc ON i.network_id = ndpc.network_id WHERE ndpc.total_down_ports > (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) FROM NetworkDownPortCounts) ORDER BY i.network_id, i.row_number_within_network_by_port_id, i.ip_address;

question: Among the ports returned by the existing “DOWN ports on host drive-59” window/running-sum analysis, list the top 10 tenants with the most such ports, showing each tenant’s ID, the total number of matching ports, and whether any of those ports have a port-security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), Drive59PortsRunningSum AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), DownDrive59PortDetails AS ( SELECT dpw.NAME, dpw.MAC_ADDRESS, dpw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpw.HOST, dpw.VIF_TYPE, dpw.window_column AS down_ports_avg_admin_state_up_window, d59.PORT_ID, d59.TENANT_ID, d59.window_column AS drive59_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN Drive59PortsRunningSum d59 ON dpw.MAC_ADDRESS = d59.MAC_ADDRESS WHERE dpw.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT * FROM DownDrive59PortDetails ORDER BY VIF_TYPE, MAC_ADDRESS, PORT_ID ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_binding FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = i.port_id LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each binding host, find the host name and the maximum DOWN-status rank (ordered by port ID within the DOWN group) among ports that are DOWN and have port security enabled, where the ports are matched to admin-up ports by MAC address. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortsWithSecurity AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, dpwb.window_column AS down_status_rank, aupws.port_security_enabled, aupws.window_column AS admin_up_row_number FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortsWithSecurity aupws ON dpwb.mac_address = aupws.mac_address WHERE aupws.port_security_enabled = 1 ORDER BY dpwb.port_id) SELECT binding_host, MAX(down_status_rank) AS max_down_status_rank FROM inner_cte GROUP BY binding_host;

question: For network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, compute the ratio of tenant `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57` “admin up with at least one IP allocation” ports (matched to DOWN ports on the same network by MAC address) to the distinct DOWN port names, and return only networks where this ratio is greater than 0.25 (also returning the underlying distinct DOWN port name count, distinct DOWN security group count, and the tenant port/IP totals used in the ratio). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH TenantUpPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), DownPortsOnNetworkWithSG AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), TenantUpPortsWithIPsOnNetwork AS ( SELECT t.port_id, t.tenant_id, t.mac_address, t.ip_allocation_count, t.subnet_id_rows FROM TenantUpPortsWithIPs t JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = t.port_id WHERE p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT d.NETWORK_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT d.NAME) AS down_port_name_count, COUNT(DISTINCT d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID) AS down_port_security_group_count, COUNT(DISTINCT t.port_id) AS tenant_up_port_count_with_ips, SUM(t.ip_allocation_count) AS tenant_up_total_ip_allocations, SUM(t.subnet_id_rows) AS tenant_up_total_subnet_id_rows FROM DownPortsOnNetworkWithSG d LEFT JOIN TenantUpPortsWithIPsOnNetwork t ON t.mac_address = d.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY d.NETWORK_ID) SELECT network_id, down_port_name_count, down_port_security_group_count, tenant_up_port_count_with_ips, tenant_up_total_ip_allocations, tenant_up_total_subnet_id_rows, (tenant_up_port_count_with_ips * 1.0 / NULLIF(down_port_name_count, 0)) AS tenant_up_to_down_name_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE down_port_name_count > 0 AND (tenant_up_port_count_with_ips * 1.0 / down_port_name_count) > 0.25;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', among the security groups whose ratio is greater than 75% of (ports that are administratively up and have at least one IP allocation) compared to (ports that are DOWN and bound to that security group), what is the maximum number of distinct IP allocation subnets (SUBNET_ID) observed on any single admin-up port associated with that security group? Return the security group ID and this maximum distinct-subnet count. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), AdminUpPortsWithIPAllocations AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT dpsg.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.port_id) AS down_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT aup.port_id) AS admin_up_port_with_ip_count FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg LEFT JOIN AdminUpPortsWithIPAllocations aup ON aup.tenant_id = dpsg.tenant_id GROUP BY dpsg.security_group_id HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT aup.port_id) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.port_id), 0)) > 0.75) , PortSubnetCounts AS ( SELECT spb.security_group_id, p.id AS port_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.subnet_id) AS distinct_subnet_count FROM ports p JOIN securitygroupportbindings spb ON spb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY spb.security_group_id, p.id ) SELECT i.security_group_id, MAX(psc.distinct_subnet_count) AS max_distinct_subnets_on_any_admin_up_port FROM inner_cte i JOIN PortSubnetCounts psc ON psc.security_group_id = i.security_group_id GROUP BY i.security_group_id;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', for each network, find the network ID and the highest DNS-records-per-max-binding ratio among its security groups (where each security group is computed only from security groups that have DOWN ports, using the ratio of total DNS record count across the tenant’s admin_state_up = 1 ports in that group divided by the maximum number of security-group bindings among those admin_state_up ports, rounded to 2 decimals).
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ) SELECT dpsg.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.port_id) AS down_port_count, MAX(au.security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_binding_count_among_admin_up_ports, SUM(au.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_record_count_for_admin_up_ports, ROUND( SUM(au.dns_record_count) / NULLIF(MAX(au.security_group_binding_count), 0), 2 ) AS dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts au ON au.port_id = dpsg.port_id AND au.tenant_id = dpsg.tenant_id WHERE dpsg.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY dpsg.security_group_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio DESC) , NetworkSecurityGroupRatios AS ( SELECT p.network_id, i.security_group_id, i.dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM inner_cte i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.security_group_id = i.security_group_id JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = sgpb.port_id ) SELECT network_id, MAX(dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio) AS max_dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM NetworkSecurityGroupRatios GROUP BY network_id;

question: For tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', using the counts of (1) administratively up ports with port security bindings and (2) DOWN ports with a standard-attributes running-sum window value, what is the maximum of these two counts? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH admin_up_port_security AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') ) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM admin_up_port_security) AS admin_up_ports_with_security_bindings_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM down_ports_window) AS down_ports_with_standardattributes_window_count FROM admin_up_port_security aups CROSS JOIN down_ports_window dpw ) SELECT MAX(cnt) AS max_of_the_two_counts FROM ( SELECT inner_cte.admin_up_ports_with_security_bindings_count AS cnt FROM inner_cte UNION ALL SELECT inner_cte.down_ports_with_standardattributes_window_count AS cnt FROM inner_cte ) t;

question: For each network, return the network ID and the maximum (across DOWN port status and device owner) distinct port count among ports bound to a security group for tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', along with (for the same network) the minimum admin_state_up and average standard_attr_id for ports bound with VIF type 'ovs' whose device_id is 'da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), OvsBindingPortStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' AND p.DEVICE_ID IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, obs.min_admin_state_up, obs.avg_standard_attr_id FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN OvsBindingPortStats obs ON psgs.port_status = obs.STATUS) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, MAX(inner_cte.port_count) AS max_distinct_port_count, MIN(inner_cte.min_admin_state_up) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = inner_cte.port_status GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID;

question: For tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', among DOWN ports on network '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d' that are bound to a security group, list each device owner and security group ID along with the device-owner-level distinct DOWN port count and minimum standard attribute ID, include how many matching DOWN ports in that network fall under each device owner and security group, and also show the overall average of these matching DOWN-port counts across all returned device-owner/security-group rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownNetworkPortDetails AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')) SELECT dnpd.DEVICE_OWNER, dnpd.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, COUNT(*) AS matching_down_ports_in_network FROM DownNetworkPortDetails dnpd JOIN PORTS p ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = dnpd.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.NETWORK_ID = dnpd.NETWORK_ID AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = dnpd.DEVICE_OWNER AND p.STATUS = dnpd.STATUS JOIN PortStatusOwnerAgg psa ON psa.port_status = dnpd.STATUS AND psa.device_owner = dnpd.DEVICE_OWNER WHERE p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY dnpd.DEVICE_OWNER, dnpd.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY matching_down_ports_in_network DESC, dnpd.DEVICE_OWNER, dnpd.SECURITY_GROUP_ID) SELECT inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER, inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.min_standard_attr_id, inner_cte.matching_down_ports_in_network, avg_stats.avg_matching_down_ports_in_network FROM inner_cte JOIN (SELECT AVG(matching_down_ports_in_network) AS avg_matching_down_ports_in_network FROM inner_cte) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1;

question: Using the existing per-(port status, device owner) aggregation that filters to standard attribute resource type 'ports' and excludes shared networks, list each (port status, device owner) with its total port count, earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, and DOWN-port security-group-binding count on network '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d'; additionally, show how far each pair’s total port count deviates from the average port count across all returned (status, owner) pairs. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWithSG AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ), DownPortsSGCounts AS ( SELECT dp.STATUS AS port_status, dp.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_network_with_sg FROM DownPortsWithSG dp GROUP BY dp.STATUS, dp.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT psoa.port_status, psoa.device_owner, psoa.port_count, psoa.earliest_standard_attr_update, dpsc.down_ports_in_network_with_sg FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psoa JOIN DownPortsSGCounts dpsc ON psoa.port_status = dpsc.port_status AND psoa.device_owner = dpsc.device_owner ORDER BY psoa.port_count DESC) , AvgPortCount AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, i.down_ports_in_network_with_sg, (i.port_count - a.avg_port_count) AS deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgPortCount a ORDER BY i.port_count DESC;

question: Among the (port status, device owner) pairs returned by the existing port aggregation (only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks), list only those pairs where more than 25% of the ports are DOWN ports on network ID '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d' that have a security-group binding. For each qualifying pair, show the total port count, the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, the count of such DOWN+security-group ports, and the resulting ratio. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWithSG AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ), DownPortsSGCounts AS ( SELECT dp.STATUS AS port_status, dp.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_network_with_sg FROM DownPortsWithSG dp GROUP BY dp.STATUS, dp.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT psoa.port_status, psoa.device_owner, psoa.port_count, psoa.earliest_standard_attr_update, dpsc.down_ports_in_network_with_sg FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psoa JOIN DownPortsSGCounts dpsc ON psoa.port_status = dpsc.port_status AND psoa.device_owner = dpsc.device_owner ORDER BY psoa.port_count DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.earliest_standard_attr_update, inner_cte.down_ports_in_network_with_sg, (inner_cte.down_ports_in_network_with_sg * 1.0 / NULLIF(inner_cte.port_count, 0)) AS down_sg_ratio FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.DEVICE_OWNER = inner_cte.device_owner AND p2.STATUS = inner_cte.port_status WHERE (inner_cte.down_ports_in_network_with_sg * 1.0 / NULLIF(inner_cte.port_count, 0)) > 0.25 GROUP BY inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.earliest_standard_attr_update, inner_cte.down_ports_in_network_with_sg ORDER BY down_sg_ratio DESC, inner_cte.port_count DESC;

question: Using the per-(DOWN status, device owner) port statistics for ports in tenant '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7' that are bound to a security group (including the matching per-status OVS-binding stats for device_id 'da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7'), list the top 10 device owners by distinct port count and indicate whether each device owner has any of those ports bound with VIF type 'ovs'. Return device owner, port status, distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, the per-status minimum admin_state_up and average standard_attr_id, and the Yes/No flag. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), OvsBindingPortStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' AND p.DEVICE_ID IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, obs.min_admin_state_up, obs.avg_standard_attr_id FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN OvsBindingPortStats obs ON psgs.port_status = obs.STATUS) SELECT i.device_owner, i.port_status, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.min_admin_state_up, i.avg_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT b2.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_bound_ports FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.DEVICE_OWNER = i.device_owner AND p2.STATUS = i.port_status LEFT JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b2 ON b2.PORT_ID = p2.ID AND b2.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' GROUP BY i.device_owner, i.port_status, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.min_admin_state_up, i.avg_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each network ID, find the network ID and the highest security-group binding count of any port in that network, considering only ports that (1) are bound to a security group, have admin_state_up = 1, and belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', and also (2) are DOWN on network ID '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH TenantAdminUpBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownNetworkPortsWithWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ), DownNetworkPortsWithWindowAndId AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, q.NAME, q.NETWORK_ID, q.MAC_ADDRESS, q.ADMIN_STATE_UP, q.STATUS, q.DEVICE_OWNER, q.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, q.window_column FROM DownNetworkPortsWithWindow q JOIN PORTS p ON p.NAME = q.NAME AND p.NETWORK_ID = q.NETWORK_ID AND p.MAC_ADDRESS = q.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = q.ADMIN_STATE_UP AND p.STATUS = q.STATUS AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = q.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT d.port_id, t.tenant_id, t.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.admin_state_up, d.status, d.device_owner, d.security_group_id, d.window_column, t.security_group_binding_count, t.dns_record_count FROM DownNetworkPortsWithWindowAndId d JOIN TenantAdminUpBoundPorts t ON d.port_id = t.port_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.port_id, d.security_group_id) SELECT network_id, MAX(security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_bindings_on_any_port FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id;

question: For DOWN ports in network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, return each port’s name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows (ordered by port ID). Also include (for the same port status and device owner) the total number of non-shared ports whose standard attribute resource type is `ports` plus the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, but only keep rows where that port_count is greater than the average port_count across all (status, device_owner) groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT sq2.NETWORK_ID, sq2.NAME AS port_name, sq2.MAC_ADDRESS, sq2.ADMIN_STATE_UP, sq2.STATUS AS port_status, sq2.DEVICE_OWNER, sq2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, sq2.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_window, sq1.port_count, sq1.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM sq2 JOIN sq1 ON sq1.port_status = sq2.STATUS AND sq1.device_owner = sq2.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY sq1.port_count DESC, sq2.NAME ) , AvgCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT port_status, device_owner, MAX(port_count) AS port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status, device_owner ) grouped_counts ) SELECT inner_cte.NETWORK_ID, inner_cte.port_name, inner_cte.MAC_ADDRESS, inner_cte.ADMIN_STATE_UP, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.DEVICE_OWNER, inner_cte.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, inner_cte.min_admin_state_up_window, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM inner_cte JOIN AvgCounts ON 1 = 1 WHERE inner_cte.port_count > (SELECT avg_port_count FROM AvgCounts) ORDER BY inner_cte.port_count DESC, inner_cte.port_name;

question: For the unified set of DOWN ports that either (a) belong to tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57` or (b) belong to network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, compute how many ports appear under each reason label, and return only those reason labels whose port count is greater than the average port count across the reason labels. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), NetworkDownPorts AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), CombinedDownPorts AS ( SELECT t.port_id AS port_identifier, t.tenant_id AS scope_id, t.mac_address, t.window_column AS window_metric, 'Tenant Filter' AS reason FROM TenantDownPorts t UNION ALL SELECT n.NAME AS port_identifier, n.NETWORK_ID AS scope_id, n.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, n.window_column AS window_metric, 'Network Filter' AS reason FROM NetworkDownPorts n ) SELECT * FROM CombinedDownPorts ORDER BY reason, scope_id, port_identifier ), ReasonCounts AS ( SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY reason ) SELECT reason, total_ports FROM ReasonCounts WHERE total_ports > (SELECT AVG(total_ports) FROM ReasonCounts) ORDER BY total_ports DESC, reason;

question: Using the unified DOWN-port result set (ports filtered by tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57` or by network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`), return each row’s port identifier, scope ID, MAC address, window metric, and reason label, and additionally compute the deviation of each row’s window metric from the overall average window metric across the entire unified result set. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), NetworkDownPorts AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), CombinedDownPorts AS ( SELECT t.port_id AS port_identifier, t.tenant_id AS scope_id, t.mac_address, t.window_column AS window_metric, 'Tenant Filter' AS reason FROM TenantDownPorts t UNION ALL SELECT n.NAME AS port_identifier, n.NETWORK_ID AS scope_id, n.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, n.window_column AS window_metric, 'Network Filter' AS reason FROM NetworkDownPorts n ) SELECT * FROM CombinedDownPorts ORDER BY reason, scope_id, port_identifier ), AverageWindowMetric AS ( SELECT AVG(window_metric) AS avg_window_metric FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_identifier, i.scope_id, i.mac_address, i.window_metric, i.reason, (i.window_metric - a.avg_window_metric) AS deviation_from_avg_window_metric FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageWindowMetric a ORDER BY i.reason, i.scope_id, i.port_identifier;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address;

question: For each VIF type among ports that are DOWN, show the VIF type, total number of distinct DOWN ports, the average of the MAC-address-based admin_state_up window metric, the maximum IP-address-based row-number window value, and the number of distinct tenants, by combining the DOWN-port MAC window results with the DOWN-port IP allocation row-number results joined on host and VIF type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortDownMacWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), PortDownIpRowNumber AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT p2.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.port_id) AS Total_Down_Ports, AVG(p1.window_column) AS Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, MAX(p2.window_column) AS Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.tenant_id) AS Distinct_Tenants FROM PortDownIpRowNumber p2 JOIN PortDownMacWindow p1 ON p1.HOST = p2.host AND p1.VIF_TYPE = p2.vif_type GROUP BY p2.vif_type ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC;

question: For DOWN ports, list the tenant ID, the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and average admin_state_up (rounded), along with each port’s security group ID and rank within that security group (by port ID), plus the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, the 2-preceding-to-2-following VIF-type window average of admin_state_up (ordered by MAC address), and the normalized ratio of that window average to the tenant’s average admin_state_up for DOWN ports.
SQL: WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), SecurityGroupPortRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPortSummary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(p.admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up_down FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT sgpr.tenant_id, tds.down_port_count, ROUND(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id, pbw.NAME AS port_name, sgpr.mac_address, pbw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, pbw.HOST AS binding_host, pbw.VIF_TYPE, pbw.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, sgpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, ROUND( pbw.window_column / NULLIF(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 0), 2 ) AS normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM SecurityGroupPortRank sgpr JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON pbw.MAC_ADDRESS = sgpr.mac_address JOIN TenantDownPortSummary tds ON tds.tenant_id = sgpr.tenant_id ORDER BY normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id;

question: For each port that is DOWN and also has admin_state_up = 1 with at least one security group binding, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within its network (ordered by port ID), the number of security group bindings, the total number of DNS records, and the DNS-records-per-security-group-binding ratio rounded to 2 decimals.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityAndDNS AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, psd.security_group_binding_count, psd.dns_record_count, ROUND(psd.dns_record_count / NULLIF(psd.security_group_binding_count, 0), 2) AS dns_records_per_security_group_binding FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortSecurityAndDNS psd ON psd.port_id = d.port_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_security_group_binding DESC, d.network_id, d.window_column;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID, name, MAC address, binding host, and VIF type, along with (1) the port’s rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID and (2) the dense rank of the port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT pbr.port_id, pbr.port_name, pbr.mac_address, pbr.binding_host, pbr.vif_type, pbr.window_column AS rank_within_down_status_by_port_id, psw.window_column AS dense_rank_by_port_security_with_2_preceding_frame FROM PortBindingRank pbr JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pbr.port_id = psw.port_id ORDER BY pbr.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within its network (ordered by port ID), the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following port (ordered by port ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsWithSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpi.port_id, dpi.tenant_id, dpi.port_name, dpi.network_id, dpi.mac_address, dpi.device_owner, dpi.ip_address, dpi.window_column AS row_num_within_network, dpsw.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, dpsw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsw.STATUS, dpsw.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_window FROM DownPortsWithIPs dpi JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityWindow dpsw ON dpi.network_id = dpsw.NETWORK_ID AND dpi.port_name = dpsw.NAME AND dpi.mac_address = dpsw.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpi.device_owner = dpsw.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY dpi.network_id, dpi.port_id;

question: For ports that are administratively up, have at least one IP allocation, and also have status DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on the port, the total number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations, and the port’s dense-rank by its port-security setting using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows, ordered by the IP allocation count descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sq1.port_id, sq1.tenant_id, sq1.mac_address, sq1.ip_allocation_count, sq1.subnet_id_rows, sq2.window_column FROM sq1 JOIN sq2 ON sq1.port_id = sq2.port_id ORDER BY sq1.ip_allocation_count DESC;

question: From the top 10 networks with the most DOWN ports, list each network ID and its DOWN-port count, and for each DOWN port show the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s row number within its network (ordered by port ID), and the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), top_networks AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_port_count FROM sq2 GROUP BY network_id ORDER BY down_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tn.network_id, tn.down_port_count, sq2.port_id, sq2.tenant_id, sq2.port_name, sq2.mac_address, sq2.device_owner, sq2.ip_address, sq2.window_column AS port_row_number_within_network, sq1.binding_host, sq1.vif_type, sq1.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM top_networks tn JOIN sq2 ON tn.network_id = sq2.network_id LEFT JOIN sq1 ON sq2.port_id = sq1.port_id ORDER BY tn.down_port_count DESC, tn.network_id, sq2.window_column, sq2.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN (including their binding host, VIF type, and rank within the DOWN status group) and that also are administratively up with at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, port name, tenant ID, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the number of IP allocations on the port, the total number of subnet-id rows from those allocations, and the port’s rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH AdminUpPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, apwi.tenant_id, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, apwi.ip_allocation_count, apwi.subnet_id_rows, dpwb.window_column FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortsWithIPs apwi ON dpwb.port_id = apwi.port_id ORDER BY dpwb.window_column, dpwb.port_id;

question: For each port that is administratively up, has at least one IP allocation, and is also in DOWN status, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations, the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the ratio of IP allocation count to that running-sum value rounded to 2 decimals.
SQL: WITH AdminUpPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT a.port_id, a.tenant_id, a.mac_address, a.ip_allocation_count, a.subnet_id_rows, d.window_column, ROUND(a.ip_allocation_count / NULLIF(d.window_column, 0), 2) AS IpAllocations_Per_WindowId FROM AdminUpPortsWithIPs a JOIN DownPortsWindow d ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY IpAllocations_Per_WindowId DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT s1.port_id, s1.tenant_id, s1.mac_address, s2.port_status, s2.ip_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, s2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.port_id = s2.port_id ORDER BY s1.port_id;

question: For active networks that have admin_state_up = 1 and at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports on that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name;

question: For ports that are DOWN and also administratively up, list the port ID, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the per-port windowed average port ID (ordered by IP address), the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the port-security-enabled ratio (enabled total divided by binding count), ordered by the ratio descending and then by IP address.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortSecurity AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total, ROUND(a.port_security_enabled_total / NULLIF(a.binding_count, 0), 2) AS Port_Security_Enabled_Ratio FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurity a ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY Port_Security_Enabled_Ratio DESC, d.ip_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, which port IDs (with their tenant ID, host, VIF type, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, and subnet ID) appear when combining (1) the row number over IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row and (2) the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_bindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), down_ports_ipavg AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpb.port_id, dpb.tenant_id, dpb.host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.ip_address, dpb.window_column AS row_number_by_ip_window, dpi.port_name, dpi.mac_address, dpi.subnet_id, dpi.window_column AS avg_port_id_by_ip_window FROM down_ports_bindings dpb JOIN down_ports_ipavg dpi ON dpb.port_id = dpi.port_id AND dpb.ip_address = dpi.ip_address;

question: For ports with status equal to 'DOWN', show the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortIpWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), DownPortNetworkRowNum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpiw.port_id, dpnr.tenant_id, dpiw.port_name, dpnr.network_id, dpiw.mac_address, dpnr.device_owner, dpiw.ip_address, dpiw.subnet_id, dpiw.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, dpnr.window_column AS row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM DownPortIpWindow dpiw JOIN DownPortNetworkRowNum dpnr ON dpiw.port_id = dpnr.port_id AND dpiw.ip_address = dpnr.ip_address ORDER BY dpnr.network_id, dpnr.window_column, dpiw.ip_address;

question: How many ports are both DOWN (with a running sum of STANDARD_ATTR_ID within each security group) and administratively up (with port security binding counts and total enabled port security), matching on port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), admin_up_ports_security AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count FROM down_ports_window dpw JOIN admin_up_ports_security aups ON dpw.port_id = aups.port_id AND dpw.tenant_id = aups.tenant_id AND dpw.mac_address = aups.mac_address;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, along with any DOWN ports on that network (port ID and MAC address), the port’s security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), and the network’s row number within its tenant (ordered by network name). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT q2.network_id, q2.network_name, q2.tenant_id, q2.admin_state_up, q2.mtu, q2.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.port_id, q1.mac_address, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = q2.network_id JOIN q1 ON q1.port_id = p.id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q2.tenant_id, q2.network_name, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column, q1.port_id;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard attribute updated_at timestamp, along with any DOWN ports on that network (port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type) and the rank of each DOWN port within its status group ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
