SQL: WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, dp.port_id, dp.port_name, dp.mac_address, dp.binding_host, dp.vif_type, dp.window_column AS down_port_rank_within_status FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.port_id = p.ID;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports, list each tenant’s ID and DOWN port count, along with their ACTIVE networks (network ID, network name, admin_state_up, MTU, standard attribute updated_at, and the row number per tenant ordered by network name) and the tenant’s DOWN ports (port ID, MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), top_tenants AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM subq1 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY down_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tt.tenant_id, tt.down_port_count, s2.network_id, s2.network_name, s2.admin_state_up, s2.mtu, s2.standard_attr_updated_at, s2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, s1.port_id, s1.mac_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type FROM top_tenants tt JOIN subq2 s2 ON s2.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id LEFT JOIN subq1 s1 ON s1.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id ORDER BY tt.down_port_count DESC, tt.tenant_id, s2.window_column, s2.network_name, s1.port_id;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, and VIF type, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group, (2) the rank of the port among DOWN ports ordered by port ID, and (3) the ratio of the running sum to the rank (rounded to 2 decimals), ordered by this ratio descending.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpb.port_name, dpsg.mac_address, dpb.binding_host, dpb.vif_type, dpsg.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, dpb.window_column AS rank_within_down_status, ROUND(dpsg.window_column / NULLIF(dpb.window_column, 0), 2) AS running_sum_to_rank_ratio FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN DownPortsWithBindings dpb ON dpsg.port_id = dpb.port_id ORDER BY running_sum_to_rank_ratio DESC, dpsg.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN but also administratively up, return the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID), the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings on the port, and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings—only including ports where port security is enabled at least once. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id;

question: For DOWN ports, considering only the first 3 ports per network (by port ID), show for each tenant and VIF type the number of such DOWN ports and the average of the 2-preceding/2-following admin_state_up window metric (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpi.tenant_id, pbw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(pbw.window_column) AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol FROM DownPortsWithIPs dpi JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON dpi.mac_address = pbw.MAC_ADDRESS WHERE dpi.window_column <= 3 GROUP BY dpi.tenant_id, pbw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, avg_admin_state_up_window_2_pre_2_fol DESC;

question: For ports with status DOWN, return (1) the number of distinct DOWN ports that are bound to a security group and the minimum standard attribute ID for each device owner, and (2) the DOWN port details (port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, and the rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID), output together in one result set. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortDetails AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpd.port_id, dpd.port_name, dpd.mac_address, dpd.binding_host, dpd.vif_type, dpd.window_column FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortDetails dpd;

question: For ports with status DOWN, return each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also include the corresponding summary for that port’s status and device owner considering only ports bound to a security group (distinct port count and minimum standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, list each device owner’s port status, distinct port count, and minimum standard attribute ID, alongside each matching port’s name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following ports ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_status, subq1.device_owner, subq1.port_count, subq1.min_standard_attr_id, subq2.NAME AS port_name, subq2.NETWORK_ID, subq2.MAC_ADDRESS, subq2.ADMIN_STATE_UP, subq2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, subq2.window_column FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.port_status = subq2.STATUS AND subq1.device_owner = subq2.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY subq1.port_count DESC, subq1.device_owner, subq2.NETWORK_ID, subq2.NAME;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin_state_up, status, device owner, binding host, VIF type, the bound security group ID, the average admin_state_up over a 2-preceding/2-following window partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address, and the minimum admin_state_up over a 3-preceding/1-following window ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), DownPortsWithSecurityGroups AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT dpb.NAME AS port_name, dpsg.NETWORK_ID, dpb.MAC_ADDRESS, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsg.STATUS, dpsg.DEVICE_OWNER, dpb.HOST AS binding_host, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpsg.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS bound_security_group_id, dpb.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, dpsg.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_portid_window FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpb JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityGroups dpsg ON dpb.NAME = dpsg.NAME AND dpb.MAC_ADDRESS = dpsg.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP = dpsg.ADMIN_STATE_UP ORDER BY dpb.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For ports that (1) are bound to a security group and have admin_state_up = 1 and (2) have status = 'DOWN', list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, the number of security group bindings for the port, the total number of DNS records associated with the port, the MAC address, the binding host, the VIF type, and the port’s rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SecurityGroupAndDnsByPort AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortBindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sgd.port_id, sgd.tenant_id, sgd.port_name, sgd.security_group_binding_count, sgd.dns_record_count, dpb.mac_address, dpb.binding_host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.window_column FROM SecurityGroupAndDnsByPort sgd JOIN DownPortBindings dpb ON sgd.port_id = dpb.port_id;

question: For ports that are bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c and have status DOWN, show the port ID, port status, allocated IP address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the dense rank of the port when ordering by its port-security setting using a window frame that includes the current row and the 2 preceding rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SG_Bound_Ports AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), Down_Ports_DenseRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sbp.port_id, sbp.port_status, sbp.ip_address, sbp.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, dpdr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_port_security_for_down_ports FROM SG_Bound_Ports sbp JOIN Down_Ports_DenseRank dpdr ON sbp.port_id = dpdr.port_id WHERE sbp.port_status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY sbp.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, which ports (by port ID) have both a security-group running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID and an IP allocation record, and what are the tenant ID, MAC address, security-group running-sum value, port name, allocated IP address, subnet ID, and the average port ID window value (ordered by IP address) for those ports? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_security_groups AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), down_ports_ip_allocations AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, dpsg.window_column AS security_group_running_sum_standard_attr_id, dpia.port_name, dpia.ip_address, dpia.subnet_id, dpia.window_column AS avg_port_id_over_ip_order FROM down_ports_security_groups dpsg JOIN down_ports_ip_allocations dpia ON dpia.port_id = dpsg.port_id AND dpia.mac_address = dpsg.mac_address;

question: For active networks, list each network’s tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up, MTU, and standard attribute updated_at (with a row number per tenant ordered by network name), and for each of those networks also show the DOWN ports on that network including port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, and the rank of each port within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPorts AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), ActiveNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE') SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, dp.port_id, dp.port_name, dp.mac_address, dp.binding_host, dp.vif_type, dp.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND p.STATUS = 'DOWN' JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.port_id = p.ID ORDER BY an.tenant_id, an.window_column, dp.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, provide the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), PortsInGivenSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), DownPortsInGivenSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, pisg.port_status, pisg.ip_address, dpsg.window_column AS down_ports_sg_running_sum_standard_attr_id, pisg.window_column AS sg_ports_network_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN PortsInGivenSecurityGroup pisg ON dpsg.port_id = pisg.port_id ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, port_status, ip_address, down_ports_sg_running_sum_standard_attr_id, sg_ports_network_running_sum_standard_attr_id FROM DownPortsInGivenSecurityGroup;

question: For each port that is both (1) DOWN with an allocated IP address and a row number within its network (ordered by port ID) and (2) bound to a security group with admin_state_up = 1, list the network ID, the per-network row number, port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the number of security group bindings for the port, and the total number of DNS records associated with the port. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH AdminUpBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.network_id, d.window_column AS down_port_row_number_in_network, d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, a.security_group_binding_count, a.dns_record_count FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN AdminUpBoundPorts a ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY d.network_id, d.window_column, d.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN but also administratively up and have at least one IP allocation, return the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), plus the port’s IP allocation count and the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH AdminUpWithIPAllocations AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsRunningStdAttrSumBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.mac_address, d.window_column, a.ip_allocation_count, a.subnet_id_rows FROM DownPortsRunningStdAttrSumBySecurityGroup d JOIN AdminUpWithIPAllocations a ON a.port_id = d.port_id ORDER BY d.tenant_id, d.port_id;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list a combined report that includes (1) each port’s name, MAC address, admin_state_up, binding host, VIF type, and the VIF-type window average of admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows ordered by MAC address), and (2) each port’s ID, name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, and its rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID, labeling each row with the metric type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWindowAvg AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), DownPortsRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), CombinedDownPortAnalytics AS ( SELECT NULL AS port_id, d1.NAME AS port_name, d1.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, d1.HOST AS binding_host, d1.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, d1.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, d1.window_column AS window_metric, 'VIF-type window avg(admin_state_up)' AS metric_type FROM DownPortsWindowAvg d1 UNION ALL SELECT d2.port_id AS port_id, d2.port_name AS port_name, d2.mac_address AS mac_address, d2.binding_host AS binding_host, d2.vif_type AS vif_type, NULL AS admin_state_up, d2.window_column AS window_metric, 'Status-group rank by port_id' AS metric_type FROM DownPortsRank d2 ) SELECT * FROM CombinedDownPortAnalytics ORDER BY vif_type, mac_address, metric_type, port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, return each port’s ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the row number of the port within its network ordered by port ID and (2) the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following port (ordered by port ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortsWithSecurityGroupWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT dpi.port_id, dpi.tenant_id, dpi.port_name, dpi.network_id, dpi.mac_address, dpsgw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsgw.STATUS, dpi.device_owner, dpsgw.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, dpi.ip_address, dpi.window_column AS network_row_number, dpsgw.window_column AS admin_state_up_min_window FROM DownPortsWithIPs dpi JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityGroupWindow dpsgw ON dpi.port_id = dpsgw.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT q2.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q2.port_status, q2.ip_address, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q2.port_id = q1.port_id ORDER BY q2.port_id;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list ports that are DOWN and also have admin_state_up = 1 and are bound to a security group, showing the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group ordered by port ID, the port name, the number of security group bindings for the port, and the total number of DNS records associated with the port. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), AdminUpPortsSecurityGroupAndDNSCounts AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name) SELECT dp.port_id, dp.tenant_id, dp.mac_address, dp.security_group_id, dp.window_column AS down_port_rank_within_security_group, au.port_name, au.security_group_binding_count, au.dns_record_count FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dp JOIN AdminUpPortsSecurityGroupAndDNSCounts au ON au.port_id = dp.port_id AND au.tenant_id = dp.tenant_id;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', return the total number of ACTIVE networks, the total number of DOWN ports (from the security-group-to-port bindings), and the average number of DOWN ports per ACTIVE network.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), ActiveNetworksByTenant AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND n.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ActiveNetworksByTenant) AS total_active_networks, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup) AS total_down_ports, ROUND( (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup) / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ActiveNetworksByTenant), 0), 2 ) AS avg_down_ports_per_active_network ;

question: For DOWN ports that belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57' and are on network ID '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d', list the port ID, tenant ID, network ID, port name, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, and security group ID, along with (1) the rank of each port within its security group ordered by port ID and (2) the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows ordered by port ID, but only for security groups that have at least 2 such DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH TenantDownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), NetworkDownPortsWithMinAdminStateWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ), SecurityGroupDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT sgpb.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS down_port_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') AND p.network_id IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') GROUP BY sgpb.security_group_id ) SELECT tdp.port_id, tdp.tenant_id, ndp.network_id, ndp.name AS port_name, tdp.mac_address, ndp.admin_state_up, ndp.status, ndp.device_owner, tdp.security_group_id, tdp.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, ndp.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_window, sgc.down_port_count FROM TenantDownPortsBySecurityGroup AS tdp JOIN NetworkDownPortsWithMinAdminStateWindow AS ndp ON tdp.security_group_id = ndp.security_group_id AND tdp.mac_address = ndp.mac_address JOIN SecurityGroupDownPortCounts AS sgc ON tdp.security_group_id = sgc.security_group_id WHERE sgc.down_port_count >= 2 ORDER BY sgc.down_port_count DESC, tdp.security_group_id, tdp.port_id;

question: For DOWN ports in network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, list each port’s name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following rows (ordered by port ID), and also show (for the same port status and device owner) the total number of non-shared ports whose standard attribute resource type is `ports` plus the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT sq2.NETWORK_ID, sq2.NAME AS port_name, sq2.MAC_ADDRESS, sq2.ADMIN_STATE_UP, sq2.STATUS AS port_status, sq2.DEVICE_OWNER, sq2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, sq2.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_window, sq1.port_count, sq1.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM sq2 JOIN sq1 ON sq1.port_status = sq2.STATUS AND sq1.device_owner = sq2.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY sq1.port_count DESC, sq2.NAME;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each DOWN port along with its security group ID and its rank within that security group (ordered by port ID), and also show (when available) the port’s IP allocation count and the number of subnet-id rows from IP allocations for administratively up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT subq1.security_group_id, subq1.port_id AS down_port_id, subq1.tenant_id, subq1.mac_address, subq1.window_column AS down_port_rank_within_security_group, subq2.ip_allocation_count, subq2.subnet_id_rows FROM subq1 LEFT JOIN subq2 ON subq1.port_id = subq2.port_id ORDER BY subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column, subq1.port_id;

question: For ports with status 'DOWN' and tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7' that are bound to a security group, and considering only port statuses that also appear among ports bound with VIF type 'ovs' for device_id 'da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7', show (by port status and device owner) the distinct port count, the minimum standard attribute ID, the minimum admin_state_up value, and the average standard_attr_id. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusOwnerSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusOvsBindingStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' AND p.DEVICE_ID IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT psosgs.port_status, psosgs.device_owner, psosgs.port_count, psosgs.min_standard_attr_id, psobs.min_admin_state_up, psobs.avg_standard_attr_id FROM PortStatusOwnerSecurityGroupStats psosgs JOIN PortStatusOvsBindingStats psobs ON psosgs.port_status = psobs.STATUS ORDER BY psosgs.port_count DESC;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each ACTIVE network (network ID, name, admin_state_up, MTU, and standard attribute updated_at with its row number within the tenant by network name) together with any DOWN ports on that network, showing each port’s ID, MAC address, security group ID, and the port’s rank within its security group ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityGroupRanks AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), ActiveTenantNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND n.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), DownTenantPortsWithNetwork AS ( SELECT psgr.port_id, psgr.tenant_id, psgr.mac_address, psgr.security_group_id, psgr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, p.network_id FROM PortSecurityGroupRanks psgr JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = psgr.port_id WHERE psgr.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, dtp.port_id, dtp.mac_address, dtp.security_group_id, dtp.port_rank_within_security_group FROM ActiveTenantNetworks atn JOIN DownTenantPortsWithNetwork dtp ON dtp.network_id = atn.network_id AND dtp.tenant_id = atn.tenant_id ORDER BY atn.tenant_id, atn.network_name, dtp.security_group_id, dtp.port_id;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', find ports that are DOWN but also have admin_state_up = 1 and are bound to a security group. SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), AdminUpPortBindingAndDNSCounts AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), DownPortsThatAreAlsoAdminUp AS ( SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, dpsg.security_group_id, dpsg.window_column, aup.port_name, aup.security_group_binding_count, aup.dns_record_count FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortBindingAndDNSCounts aup ON dpsg.port_id = aup.port_id AND dpsg.tenant_id = aup.tenant_id ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, security_group_id, window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, port_name, security_group_binding_count, dns_record_count FROM DownPortsThatAreAlsoAdminUp ORDER BY security_group_id, port_id;

question: For tenant ID `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, list ports that are DOWN but also have admin state up and at least one IP allocation; for each such port, return the tenant ID, port ID, MAC address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the number of IP allocations on the port, and the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortIpAllocationStats AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsSecurityGroupWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT dpsgw.tenant_id, dpsgw.port_id, dpsgw.mac_address, dpsgw.window_column, pis.ip_allocation_count, pis.subnet_id_rows FROM DownPortsSecurityGroupWindow dpsgw JOIN PortIpAllocationStats pis ON pis.port_id = dpsgw.port_id AND pis.tenant_id = dpsgw.tenant_id WHERE pis.ip_allocation_count >= 1 ORDER BY dpsgw.window_column DESC, dpsgw.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and security group ID, along with (1) the port’s rank within its security group when ordered by port ID and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within the same security group ordered by standard attribute ID. SQL: WITH ports_rank_within_sg AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), ports_running_sum_std_attr AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT prws.port_id, prws.tenant_id, prws.mac_address, prws.security_group_id, prws.window_column AS rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, prssa.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group FROM ports_rank_within_sg prws JOIN ports_running_sum_std_attr prssa ON prssa.port_id = prws.port_id AND prssa.tenant_id = prws.tenant_id AND prssa.mac_address = prws.mac_address;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', list each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and security group ID, along with (1) the port’s rank within its security group when ordered by port ID and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group ordered by standard attribute ID. SQL: WITH RankedPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), RunningSumStandardAttrIdBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ) SELECT r.port_id, r.tenant_id, r.mac_address, r.security_group_id, r.window_column AS rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, s.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group FROM RankedPortsBySecurityGroup r JOIN RunningSumStandardAttrIdBySecurityGroup s ON s.port_id = r.port_id AND s.tenant_id = r.tenant_id AND s.mac_address = r.mac_address;

question: For each DOWN port status and device owner among ports bound to a security group for tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', return the distinct port count and minimum standard attribute ID, along with (for the same port status) the minimum admin_state_up and average standard_attr_id for ports bound with VIF type 'ovs' whose device_id is 'da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7'. SQL: WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), OvsBindingPortStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) AS min_admin_state_up, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE b.VIF_TYPE = 'ovs' AND p.DEVICE_ID IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, obs.min_admin_state_up, obs.avg_standard_attr_id FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN OvsBindingPortStats obs ON psgs.port_status = obs.STATUS;

question: For tenant ID `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`, list each port that is administratively up and also has status DOWN, showing the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of port security bindings on the port, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityAgg AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') ) SELECT psa.port_id, psa.tenant_id, psa.mac_address, psa.binding_count, psa.port_security_enabled_total, dpw.window_column FROM PortSecurityAgg psa JOIN DownPortsWindow dpw ON psa.port_id = dpw.port_id AND psa.tenant_id = dpw.tenant_id AND psa.mac_address = dpw.mac_address;

question: For tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57', for each security group that has ports in DOWN status, list the security group ID, the number of distinct DOWN ports in that security group, the maximum number of security-group bindings among the tenant’s admin_state_up = 1 ports in that group, the total DNS record count across those admin_state_up ports, and the DNS-records-per-max-binding ratio rounded to 2 decimals.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ) SELECT dpsg.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.port_id) AS down_port_count, MAX(au.security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_binding_count_among_admin_up_ports, SUM(au.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_record_count_for_admin_up_ports, ROUND( SUM(au.dns_record_count) / NULLIF(MAX(au.security_group_binding_count), 0), 2 ) AS dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts au ON au.port_id = dpsg.port_id AND au.tenant_id = dpsg.tenant_id WHERE dpsg.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY dpsg.security_group_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio DESC;

question: For DOWN ports on network ID '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d', restrict to only those security groups that also contain DOWN ports owned by tenant ID '98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57'. For the matching security groups, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the security group ID, the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following ports (ordered by port ID), plus the tenant’s port ID, tenant ID, and that port’s rank within its security group when ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH TenantDownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), NetworkDownPortsWithAdminStateWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT n.NAME, n.NETWORK_ID, n.MAC_ADDRESS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.STATUS, n.DEVICE_OWNER, n.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, n.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_window_3_preceding_1_following, t.port_id, t.tenant_id, t.window_column AS rank_within_security_group_by_port_id FROM NetworkDownPortsWithAdminStateWindow AS n JOIN TenantDownPortsBySecurityGroup AS t ON n.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = t.security_group_id ORDER BY n.NETWORK_ID, n.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, t.port_id;

question: For network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, summarize (1) how many distinct DOWN port names and distinct bound security group IDs exist, and (2) among ports on that same network that are administratively up, belong to tenant `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57`, and have at least one IP allocation, report the number of such ports plus their total IP allocation count and total subnet_id row count (joining the two port sets by MAC address). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH TenantUpPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), DownPortsOnNetworkWithSG AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')), TenantUpPortsWithIPsOnNetwork AS ( SELECT t.port_id, t.tenant_id, t.mac_address, t.ip_allocation_count, t.subnet_id_rows FROM TenantUpPortsWithIPs t JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = t.port_id WHERE p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') ) SELECT d.NETWORK_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT d.NAME) AS down_port_name_count, COUNT(DISTINCT d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID) AS down_port_security_group_count, COUNT(DISTINCT t.port_id) AS tenant_up_port_count_with_ips, SUM(t.ip_allocation_count) AS tenant_up_total_ip_allocations, SUM(t.subnet_id_rows) AS tenant_up_total_subnet_id_rows FROM DownPortsOnNetworkWithSG d LEFT JOIN TenantUpPortsWithIPsOnNetwork t ON t.mac_address = d.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY d.NETWORK_ID;

question: For instances with display name "forge" that are in the "shelved_offloaded" VM state and have memory (MB) greater than the average "forge" memory (MB) in their availability zone, list the instance details (ID, UUID, user ID, project ID, hostname, VM/power state, memory, vCPUs, availability zone, instance-info-cache ID and network info, and the per-project minimum memory window value) along with the "shelved_offloaded" migration summary for completed migrations (minimum instance memory, total migration memory processed, and whether any related instances have a non-deleted network info cache record). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT i.ID AS instance_id, i.UUID AS instance_uuid, i.USER_ID, i.PROJECT_ID, i.HOSTNAME, i.VM_STATE, i.POWER_STATE, i.MEMORY_MB, i.VCPUS, i.AVAILABILITY_ZONE, c.ID AS info_cache_id, c.NETWORK_INFO, MIN(i.MEMORY_MB) OVER (PARTITION BY i.PROJECT_ID ORDER BY i.PROJECT_ID) AS window_column FROM INSTANCES AS i JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS c ON i.UUID = c.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i.DISPLAY_NAME = 'forge'), ZoneAverages AS ( SELECT i2.AVAILABILITY_ZONE, AVG(i2.MEMORY_MB * 1.0) AS avg_zone_memory_mb FROM INSTANCES AS i2 WHERE i2.DISPLAY_NAME = 'forge' GROUP BY i2.AVAILABILITY_ZONE ) SELECT inner_cte.instance_id, inner_cte.instance_uuid, inner_cte.USER_ID, inner_cte.PROJECT_ID, inner_cte.HOSTNAME, inner_cte.VM_STATE, inner_cte.POWER_STATE, inner_cte.MEMORY_MB, inner_cte.VCPUS, inner_cte.AVAILABILITY_ZONE, inner_cte.info_cache_id, inner_cte.NETWORK_INFO, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte JOIN ZoneAverages za ON za.AVAILABILITY_ZONE = inner_cte.AVAILABILITY_ZONE WHERE inner_cte.MEMORY_MB > za.avg_zone_memory_mb), q2 AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT MIN(i.MEMORY_MB) AS min_instance_memory_mb, SUM(m.MEMORY_PROCESSED) AS total_migration_memory_processed FROM MIGRATIONS m JOIN INSTANCES i ON m.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES ic ON i.UUID = ic.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed' AND i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' ) SELECT i.VM_STATE AS vm_state, inner_cte.min_instance_memory_mb, inner_cte.total_migration_memory_processed, CASE WHEN EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM MIGRATIONS m2 JOIN INSTANCES i2 ON m2.INSTANCE_UUID = i2.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES ic2 ON i2.UUID = ic2.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m2.STATUS = 'completed' AND i2.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' AND ic2.DELETED = 0 ) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_network_info_cache FROM inner_cte JOIN INSTANCES i ON i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' GROUP BY i.VM_STATE, inner_cte.min_instance_memory_mb, inner_cte.total_migration_memory_processed) SELECT q1.instance_id, q1.instance_uuid, q1.user_id, q1.project_id, q1.hostname, q1.vm_state, q1.power_state, q1.memory_mb, q1.vcpus, q1.availability_zone, q1.info_cache_id, q1.network_info, q1.window_column AS min_memory_mb_within_project, q2.min_instance_memory_mb AS shelved_offloaded_min_instance_memory_mb, q2.total_migration_memory_processed, q2.has_network_info_cache FROM q1 LEFT JOIN q2 ON q2.vm_state = q1.vm_state WHERE q1.vm_state = 'shelved_offloaded' ORDER BY q1.availability_zone, q1.project_id, q1.instance_id;

question: For completed migrations (where the instance info cache row is not deleted) and for instances in availability zone “flare3” whose memory_mb is above the overall flare3 average, return the migration ID, source/destination compute, instance display name, the migration’s rank within the completed status group (ordered by migration ID), the instance’s memory (MB) and its deviation from the average memory of instances involved in completed migrations, along with the matching flare3 instance UUID, VM state, memory_mb, cached network_info JSON, and the 2-preceding/2-following windowed average of memory_mb (partitioned by VM state and ordered by memory_mb). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH CompletedMigrations AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT m.ID AS migration_id, m.SOURCE_COMPUTE, m.DEST_COMPUTE, i.DISPLAY_NAME AS instance_display_name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.STATUS ORDER BY m.ID) AS window_column FROM MIGRATIONS AS m JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON m.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS ic ON i.UUID = ic.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed' AND ic.DELETED = 0 ), InstanceMemory AS ( SELECT inner_cte.migration_id, inner_cte.SOURCE_COMPUTE, inner_cte.DEST_COMPUTE, inner_cte.instance_display_name, inner_cte.window_column, i.MEMORY_MB AS instance_memory_mb FROM inner_cte JOIN MIGRATIONS m ON m.ID = inner_cte.migration_id JOIN INSTANCES i ON i.UUID = m.INSTANCE_UUID ), AverageMemory AS ( SELECT AVG(instance_memory_mb) AS avg_instance_memory_mb FROM InstanceMemory ) SELECT im.migration_id, im.SOURCE_COMPUTE, im.DEST_COMPUTE, im.instance_display_name, im.window_column AS rank_within_status, im.instance_memory_mb, (im.instance_memory_mb - am.avg_instance_memory_mb) AS deviation_from_avg_instance_memory_mb FROM InstanceMemory im CROSS JOIN AverageMemory am ORDER BY im.migration_id ), Flare3HighMemInstances AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT i.uuid, i.display_name, i.vm_state, i.memory_mb, c.network_info, AVG(i.memory_mb) OVER ( PARTITION BY i.vm_state ORDER BY i.memory_mb ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM instances AS i JOIN instance_info_caches AS c ON i.uuid = c.instance_uuid WHERE i.availability_zone = 'flare3' ORDER BY i.memory_mb ) SELECT inner_cte.uuid, inner_cte.display_name, inner_cte.vm_state, inner_cte.memory_mb, inner_cte.network_info, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.memory_mb > (SELECT AVG(memory_mb) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY inner_cte.memory_mb ) SELECT cm.migration_id, cm.SOURCE_COMPUTE, cm.DEST_COMPUTE, cm.instance_display_name, cm.rank_within_status, cm.instance_memory_mb, cm.deviation_from_avg_instance_memory_mb, f.uuid AS flare3_instance_uuid, f.vm_state AS flare3_vm_state, f.memory_mb AS flare3_memory_mb, f.network_info AS flare3_network_info, f.window_column AS flare3_windowed_avg_memory_mb FROM CompletedMigrations cm JOIN Flare3HighMemInstances f ON f.display_name = cm.instance_display_name ORDER BY cm.migration_id, f.memory_mb;

question: For confirmed migrations and for instances whose display name is 'forge', return a combined report (joined by instance display name) that includes the migration status, source and destination compute hosts, the instance display name and network_info, the dense rank within each migration status plus the overall average dense-rank across confirmed migrations and each row’s deviation from that average; and also includes the forge instance UUID, VM state, memory (MB), vCPUs, instance-extra ID and created timestamp, cached network_info JSON, the minimum instance-extra ID in a 3-preceding/1-following window ordered by memory, and whether the instance has any deleted instance-extra record. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH confirmed_migrations AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT m.status, m.source_compute, m.dest_compute, i.display_name, ic.network_info, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.status ORDER BY m.status) AS window_column FROM MIGRATIONS AS m JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON m.instance_uuid = i.uuid JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS ic ON i.uuid = ic.instance_uuid WHERE m.status = 'confirmed'), avg_rank AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT c.status, c.source_compute, c.dest_compute, c.display_name, c.network_info, c.window_column, a.avg_window_column, (c.window_column - a.avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_avg_dense_rank FROM inner_cte c CROSS JOIN avg_rank a), forge_instances AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT i.UUID AS instance_uuid, i.DISPLAY_NAME AS display_name, i.VM_STATE AS vm_state, i.MEMORY_MB AS memory_mb, i.VCPUS AS vcpus, ie.ID AS instance_extra_id, ie.CREATED_AT AS instance_extra_created_at, iic.NETWORK_INFO AS network_info, MIN(ie.ID) OVER ( ORDER BY i.MEMORY_MB ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM INSTANCES AS i JOIN INSTANCE_EXTRA AS ie ON ie.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS iic ON iic.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID WHERE i.DISPLAY_NAME = 'forge' ) SELECT ic.instance_uuid, ic.display_name, ic.vm_state, ic.memory_mb, ic.vcpus, ic.instance_extra_id, ic.instance_extra_created_at, ic.network_info, ic.window_column, CASE WHEN EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM INSTANCE_EXTRA ie2 JOIN INSTANCES i2 ON i2.UUID = ie2.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i2.UUID = ic.instance_uuid AND ie2.DELETED <> 0 ) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_deleted_instance_extra FROM inner_cte ic) SELECT cm.status AS migration_status, cm.source_compute, cm.dest_compute, cm.display_name AS migration_instance_display_name, cm.network_info AS migration_network_info, cm.window_column AS migration_dense_rank_within_status, cm.avg_window_column AS avg_migration_dense_rank_across_confirmed, cm.deviation_from_avg_dense_rank, fi.instance_uuid AS forge_instance_uuid, fi.display_name AS forge_display_name, fi.vm_state AS forge_vm_state, fi.memory_mb AS forge_memory_mb, fi.vcpus AS forge_vcpus, fi.instance_extra_id AS forge_instance_extra_id, fi.instance_extra_created_at AS forge_instance_extra_created_at, fi.network_info AS forge_network_info, fi.window_column AS forge_min_instance_extra_id_window, fi.has_deleted_instance_extra FROM confirmed_migrations cm JOIN forge_instances fi ON fi.display_name = cm.display_name;

question: Find non-deleted instances in the “shelved_offloaded” VM state that also have a completed migration whose migration ID is greater than the average migration ID among all completed migrations. For those instances, show the instance UUID, display name, power state, system metadata key and value, cached network_info JSON, and the per-key row number (ordered by instance UUID); also include, per metadata key, the total number of rows for that key and the average power state across that key, and do not repeat the metadata key if it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH shelved_metadata AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT i.UUID AS instance_uuid, i.DISPLAY_NAME AS display_name, i.POWER_STATE AS power_state, ism.KEY AS metadata_key, ism.VALUE AS metadata_value, iic.NETWORK_INFO AS network_info, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ism.KEY ORDER BY i.UUID) AS window_column FROM INSTANCES AS i JOIN INSTANCE_SYSTEM_METADATA AS ism ON ism.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS iic ON iic.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID WHERE i.DELETED = 0 AND i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded') SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(metadata_key) OVER (ORDER BY metadata_key, instance_uuid) = metadata_key THEN NULL ELSE metadata_key END AS metadata_key, instance_uuid, display_name, power_state, metadata_value, network_info, window_column, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY metadata_key) AS total_rows_per_key, AVG(power_state) OVER (PARTITION BY metadata_key) AS avg_power_state_per_key FROM inner_cte ORDER BY metadata_key, instance_uuid ), high_completed_migrations AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT m.ID AS migration_id, i.DISPLAY_NAME AS instance_display_name, i.AVAILABILITY_ZONE AS instance_availability_zone, m.STATUS AS migration_status, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.STATUS ORDER BY m.ID) AS window_column FROM MIGRATIONS AS m JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON m.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_EXTRA AS ie ON i.UUID = ie.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed') SELECT inner_cte.migration_id, inner_cte.instance_display_name, inner_cte.instance_availability_zone, inner_cte.migration_status, inner_cte.window_column FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.migration_id > (SELECT AVG(m2.ID * 1.0) FROM MIGRATIONS AS m2 WHERE m2.STATUS = 'completed') ORDER BY inner_cte.migration_id ), high_completed_migration_instances AS ( SELECT DISTINCT m.INSTANCE_UUID AS instance_uuid FROM MIGRATIONS AS m WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed' AND m.INSTANCE_UUID IN ( SELECT i.UUID FROM INSTANCES AS i WHERE i.DELETED = 0 AND i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' ) AND m.ID IN (SELECT migration_id FROM high_completed_migrations) ) SELECT sm.metadata_key, sm.instance_uuid, sm.display_name, sm.power_state, sm.metadata_value, sm.network_info, sm.window_column, sm.total_rows_per_key, sm.avg_power_state_per_key FROM shelved_metadata AS sm WHERE sm.instance_uuid IN (SELECT instance_uuid FROM high_completed_migration_instances) ORDER BY sm.metadata_key, sm.instance_uuid;

question: How many completed migrations involve instances whose display name is among the “shelved_offloaded” instances with total memory greater than 50000 MB and also above the average total memory of those qualifying instances, and how many such high-memory shelved instance display names are there? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH completed_migration_memory_deviation AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT m.ID AS migration_id, m.SOURCE_COMPUTE, m.DEST_COMPUTE, i.DISPLAY_NAME AS instance_display_name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY m.STATUS ORDER BY m.ID) AS window_column FROM MIGRATIONS AS m JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON m.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES AS ic ON i.UUID = ic.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed' AND ic.DELETED = 0 ), InstanceMemory AS ( SELECT inner_cte.migration_id, inner_cte.SOURCE_COMPUTE, inner_cte.DEST_COMPUTE, inner_cte.instance_display_name, inner_cte.window_column, i.MEMORY_MB AS instance_memory_mb FROM inner_cte JOIN MIGRATIONS m ON m.ID = inner_cte.migration_id JOIN INSTANCES i ON i.UUID = m.INSTANCE_UUID ), AverageMemory AS ( SELECT AVG(instance_memory_mb) AS avg_instance_memory_mb FROM InstanceMemory ) SELECT im.migration_id, im.SOURCE_COMPUTE, im.DEST_COMPUTE, im.instance_display_name, im.window_column AS rank_within_status, im.instance_memory_mb, (im.instance_memory_mb - am.avg_instance_memory_mb) AS deviation_from_avg_instance_memory_mb FROM InstanceMemory im CROSS JOIN AverageMemory am ORDER BY im.migration_id ), high_memory_shelved_instances AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT i.DISPLAY_NAME, SUM(i.MEMORY_MB) AS total_memory_mb FROM INSTANCE_EXTRA ie JOIN INSTANCES i ON ie.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_SYSTEM_METADATA ism ON i.UUID = ism.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' GROUP BY i.DISPLAY_NAME HAVING SUM(i.MEMORY_MB) > 50000) SELECT inner_cte.DISPLAY_NAME, inner_cte.total_memory_mb FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.total_memory_mb > (SELECT AVG(inner_cte.total_memory_mb * 1.0) FROM inner_cte) ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cmd.migration_id) AS completed_migrations_for_high_memory_shelved_instances_count, COUNT(DISTINCT hms.DISPLAY_NAME) AS high_memory_shelved_instance_display_names_count FROM completed_migration_memory_deviation cmd JOIN high_memory_shelved_instances hms ON cmd.instance_display_name = hms.DISPLAY_NAME;

question: For instances that are not deleted and whose display names are in the top 10 by number of network info cache records, show (for their completed migrations where the VM state is “shelved_offloaded”) the migration status, source compute, destination compute, instance UUID, display name, instance memory (MB), system metadata key/value, the windowed minimum memory (MB) over 3 preceding and 1 following migration rows (ordered by migration ID), the overall average of that windowed minimum and each row’s deviation from it, along with the cache record count, the overall average cache record count across the top 10, and each display name’s deviation from that cache-record average. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT m.status, m.source_compute, m.dest_compute, m.instance_uuid, i.display_name, i.memory_mb, ism.key, ism.value, MIN(i.memory_mb) OVER ( ORDER BY m.id ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM migrations AS m JOIN instances AS i ON m.instance_uuid = i.uuid JOIN instance_system_metadata AS ism ON i.uuid = ism.instance_uuid WHERE m.status = 'completed' AND i.vm_state = 'shelved_offloaded' ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS avg_window_min_memory_mb FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.status, ic.source_compute, ic.dest_compute, ic.instance_uuid, ic.display_name, ic.memory_mb, ic.key, ic.value, ic.window_column, av.avg_window_min_memory_mb, (ic.window_column - av.avg_window_min_memory_mb) AS deviation_from_avg_window_min FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN avg_cte av ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT i.DISPLAY_NAME, COUNT(iic.ID) AS cache_records FROM INSTANCE_EXTRA ie JOIN INSTANCES i ON ie.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_INFO_CACHES iic ON i.UUID = iic.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i.DELETED = 0 GROUP BY i.DISPLAY_NAME ORDER BY cache_records DESC LIMIT 10), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(cache_records) AS avg_cache_records FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.DISPLAY_NAME, ic.cache_records, ac.avg_cache_records, (ic.cache_records - ac.avg_cache_records) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN avg_cte ac ORDER BY ic.cache_records DESC ) SELECT q1.status AS migration_status, q1.source_compute, q1.dest_compute, q1.instance_uuid, q1.display_name, q1.memory_mb, q1.key AS system_metadata_key, q1.value AS system_metadata_value, q1.window_column AS window_min_memory_mb, q1.avg_window_min_memory_mb, q1.deviation_from_avg_window_min, q2.cache_records, q2.avg_cache_records, q2.deviation_from_avg AS cache_records_deviation_from_avg FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.display_name = q2.DISPLAY_NAME JOIN instances i ON i.uuid = q1.instance_uuid WHERE i.DELETED = 0 ORDER BY q2.cache_records DESC, q1.instance_uuid;

question: List all instance-related rows that either (a) are for instances with display name 'forge' and have system metadata (including instance UUID, metadata key/value, the row number ordered by metadata key using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, and instance memory in MB) where the instance memory is greater than 16000 MB, OR (b) are for instances with a completed migration where the migration’s processed memory share (memory_processed divided by memory_total) is greater than 75%, returning the instance UUID and a reason for inclusion; for the migration-based rows, only include instances whose display name is 'forge'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH ForgeMetadata AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT i.UUID, ism.KEY, ism.VALUE, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY ism.KEY ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING) AS window_column FROM INSTANCES AS i JOIN INSTANCE_SYSTEM_METADATA AS ism ON i.UUID = ism.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i.DISPLAY_NAME = 'forge' ) SELECT inner_cte.UUID, inner_cte.KEY, inner_cte.VALUE, inner_cte.window_column, i.MEMORY_MB FROM inner_cte JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON i.UUID = inner_cte.UUID WHERE i.MEMORY_MB > 16000 ), CompletedMigrationHighProcessed AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT i.display_name, i.availability_zone, m.status, m.migration_type, i.uuid, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY i.uuid ORDER BY i.uuid) AS window_column FROM instances AS i JOIN migrations AS m ON i.uuid = m.instance_uuid WHERE m.status = 'completed' ) SELECT inner_cte.display_name, inner_cte.availability_zone, inner_cte.status, inner_cte.migration_type, inner_cte.uuid, inner_cte.window_column, (m.memory_processed * 1.0 / NULLIF(m.memory_total, 0)) AS memory_processed_ratio FROM inner_cte JOIN migrations AS m ON m.instance_uuid = inner_cte.uuid AND m.status = inner_cte.status AND m.migration_type = inner_cte.migration_type WHERE (m.memory_processed * 1.0 / NULLIF(m.memory_total, 0)) > 0.75 ), CombinedInstanceSignals AS ( SELECT fm.UUID AS uuid, fm.KEY AS signal_key, fm.VALUE AS signal_value, fm.window_column AS signal_window_column, fm.MEMORY_MB AS memory_mb, 'Forge metadata (memory > 16000MB)' AS reason, NULL AS display_name, NULL AS availability_zone, NULL AS migration_status, NULL AS migration_type, NULL AS migration_window_column, NULL AS memory_processed_ratio FROM ForgeMetadata fm UNION ALL SELECT cm.uuid AS uuid, NULL AS signal_key, NULL AS signal_value, NULL AS signal_window_column, NULL AS memory_mb, 'Completed migration (memory processed ratio > 0.75)' AS reason, cm.display_name, cm.availability_zone, cm.status AS migration_status, cm.migration_type, cm.window_column AS migration_window_column, cm.memory_processed_ratio FROM CompletedMigrationHighProcessed cm WHERE cm.display_name = 'forge' ) SELECT * FROM CombinedInstanceSignals ORDER BY uuid, reason;

question: For completed migrations, list the migration details (migration id, instance UUID, migration type, source compute, destination compute, destination host, instance display name, VM state, instance memory MB, vCPUs, instance extra id, migration memory total, and the per-migration-type minimum memory total window column), but only for instances in the “shelved_offloaded” VM state whose total instance memory (summed across system metadata entries) is greater than 50000 MB and also greater than the average of those qualifying totals; additionally compute the ratio of migration MEMORY_TOTAL to that instance total memory.
SQL: WITH mem_over_avg AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT i.DISPLAY_NAME, SUM(i.MEMORY_MB) AS total_memory_mb FROM INSTANCE_EXTRA ie JOIN INSTANCES i ON ie.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_SYSTEM_METADATA ism ON i.UUID = ism.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE i.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' GROUP BY i.DISPLAY_NAME HAVING SUM(i.MEMORY_MB) > 50000) SELECT inner_cte.DISPLAY_NAME, inner_cte.total_memory_mb FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.total_memory_mb > (SELECT AVG(inner_cte.total_memory_mb * 1.0) FROM inner_cte)), completed_migrations AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT m.ID AS migration_id, m.INSTANCE_UUID, m.MIGRATION_TYPE, m.SOURCE_COMPUTE, m.DEST_COMPUTE, m.DEST_HOST, i.DISPLAY_NAME, i.VM_STATE, i.MEMORY_MB, i.VCPUS, ie.ID AS instance_extra_id, m.MEMORY_TOTAL, MIN(m.MEMORY_TOTAL) OVER (PARTITION BY m.MIGRATION_TYPE ORDER BY m.MIGRATION_TYPE) AS window_column FROM MIGRATIONS AS m JOIN INSTANCES AS i ON m.INSTANCE_UUID = i.UUID JOIN INSTANCE_EXTRA AS ie ON i.UUID = ie.INSTANCE_UUID WHERE m.STATUS = 'completed' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(MIGRATION_TYPE) OVER (ORDER BY MIGRATION_TYPE, migration_id) = MIGRATION_TYPE THEN NULL ELSE MIGRATION_TYPE END AS migration_type, migration_id, INSTANCE_UUID, SOURCE_COMPUTE, DEST_COMPUTE, DEST_HOST, DISPLAY_NAME, VM_STATE, MEMORY_MB, VCPUS, instance_extra_id, MEMORY_TOTAL, window_column FROM inner_cte ORDER BY MIGRATION_TYPE, migration_id), filtered_completed_migrations AS ( SELECT cm.migration_type, cm.migration_id, cm.INSTANCE_UUID, cm.SOURCE_COMPUTE, cm.DEST_COMPUTE, cm.DEST_HOST, cm.DISPLAY_NAME, cm.VM_STATE, cm.MEMORY_MB, cm.VCPUS, cm.instance_extra_id, cm.MEMORY_TOTAL, cm.window_column, moa.total_memory_mb FROM completed_migrations cm JOIN mem_over_avg moa ON cm.DISPLAY_NAME = moa.DISPLAY_NAME WHERE cm.VM_STATE = 'shelved_offloaded' ) SELECT fcm.migration_type, fcm.migration_id, fcm.INSTANCE_UUID, fcm.SOURCE_COMPUTE, fcm.DEST_COMPUTE, fcm.DEST_HOST, fcm.DISPLAY_NAME, fcm.VM_STATE, fcm.MEMORY_MB, fcm.VCPUS, fcm.instance_extra_id, fcm.MEMORY_TOTAL, fcm.window_column, fcm.total_memory_mb, ROUND(fcm.MEMORY_TOTAL / NULLIF(fcm.total_memory_mb, 0), 4) AS migration_memory_to_instance_total_memory_ratio FROM filtered_completed_migrations fcm ORDER BY fcm.migration_type, fcm.migration_id;

question: For availability zone 'flare3', what is the highest migration rank among migrations with status 'completed', and what is the maximum (across key names) of the per-key maximum total vCPUs for any single instance in 'flare3' (where total vCPUs is computed as SUM(vcpus) over joined system metadata rows)? Do not return any rounded answers.
